Section 8: Demographic Information. This section asks about your ethnicity, sex, and race.
   Demographic Information of Borrower
The purpose of collecting this information is to help ensure that all applicants are treated fairly and that the housing needs of communities and neighborhoods are being fulfilled. For
residential mortgage lending, Federal law requires that we ask applicants for their demographic information (ethnicity, sex, and race) in order to monitor our compliance with equal
credit opportunity, fair housing, and home mortgage disclosure laws. You are not required to provide this information, but are encouraged to do so. You may select one or more
designations for "Ethnicity" and one or more designations for "Race." The law provides that we may not discriminate on the basis of this information, or on whether you choose to
provide it. However, if you choose not to provide the information and you have made this application in person, Federal regulations require us to note your ethnicity, sex, and race on
the basis of visual observation or surname. The law also provides that we may not discriminate on the basis of age or marital status information you provide in this application. If you
do not wish to provide some or all of this information, please check below.

Partial Payment and Suspense Account Policy
PARTIAL PAYMENT AND SUSPENSE ACCOUNT POLICY (DISCLOSURE TO BORROWER)
Loan #1234567890 · ABC Mortgage Company · 11/19/2024
Doc. LN-1137 · Version 2.3 · Effective Date 08/24/2024



This policy explains how payments received on loan number 1234567890 are applied, what happens when an amount received is less than a full
contractual payment, how funds held in suspense are treated, and how you may direct an additional amount toward principal. The partial payment policy
applicable to your loan is also stated on your Closing Disclosure, and the entry on that document controls in the event of any difference. This statement
is furnished for your convenience so that the treatment of every payment you make on the property at 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345 is clear
from the outset. A copy of this document is retained in the file maintained for loan number 1234567890.

1.0 What Constitutes a Full Payment
A full contractual payment consists of the scheduled principal and interest, plus the monthly escrow deposit where an escrow account is maintained, plus any
other recurring amount identified on your periodic statement, such as an optional product premium you have elected. The total appears on your billing
statement as the amount due. Any remittance below that total is a partial payment regardless of how close it comes to the amount due.

Amounts past due from a prior period are added to the current amount due. Where more than one payment is outstanding, the total due reflects each unpaid
installment together with any late charge properly assessed, and a remittance sufficient to cover only one installment is applied to the oldest outstanding
installment first.

2.0 Computation of Time Periods
Unless a particular statute, regulation, or provision states otherwise, a period expressed in days is measured in calendar days, the day of the act or event that
starts the period is excluded, and the last day is included. Where the last day falls on a Saturday, a Sunday, or a legal public holiday, the period runs to the end
of the next day that is not one of those days.

Several requirements applicable to residential mortgage transactions are measured in business days, and the definition of a business day differs among them:
one rule counts days on which our offices are open for substantially all business, while another counts all calendar days except Sundays and legal public
holidays. Where a specific count controls a right or a deadline, it is stated in the provision that establishes it.

Where a period is measured from the delivery of a document, delivery by mail is generally presumed to occur three business days after mailing unless earlier
receipt is documented. Because these conventions determine real deadlines in your transaction, confirm the applicable dates with us or with your settlement
agent rather than estimating them.

3.0 What Happens to a Partial Payment
Where the servicer accepts a partial payment, the funds are ordinarily placed in a suspense or unapplied-funds account rather than applied immediately to the
loan. Funds remain in suspense until enough has accumulated to make a full contractual payment, at which point the full amount is applied in the standard
order and credited as of the date the account reached that total.

Funds held in suspense do not reduce the principal balance and do not stop the accrual of interest. Your periodic statement identifies any amount held in
suspense so that the status of the account is visible to you. If you prefer that a partial remittance be returned rather than held, notify the servicer at (555)
555-0120 at the time the payment is made.

4.0 Communication Preferences
You may tell us how you prefer to be reached, and we will honor a stated preference where the nature of the communication and applicable law permit. Certain
communications must be delivered in a specific manner regardless of preference, and those are sent by the required method even where you have asked to be
contacted only in another way.

Marketing communications are distinct from servicing communications. You may opt out of marketing by contacting us at (555) 555-0120 or by following the
instructions contained in the communication itself, and doing so does not affect the delivery of statements, disclosures, escrow analyses, or any other
communication concerning the administration of loan number 1234567890.

Where you have asked to receive communications electronically, keep the electronic address on file current and add our sending address to the list of
permitted senders in your mail application, so that a notice is not diverted to a junk folder. A notice diverted in that manner remains effective as of the date it
was sent.

5.0 Effect of Accepting a Payment
Acceptance of a partial payment, or of a payment tendered after the due date, does not waive the requirement that each installment be paid in full when due
and does not establish a course of dealing that alters the terms of the note. The servicer may accept a partial payment in one month and decline to accept one
in the next without notice, subject to the disclosed policy and applicable law.

A remittance marked "paid in full," or accompanied by a restrictive endorsement or a condition, may be accepted and processed without being bound by the
notation, and no such notation operates as an accord and satisfaction unless the servicer agrees in a separate writing signed by an authorized officer. If you
intend to satisfy the loan in full, request a payoff statement and remit in accordance with it.

6.0 Records and Recordkeeping
We retain the records relating to this transaction, including the loan documents, disclosures, notices, and correspondence, for the periods required by
applicable law and by our own records-management schedule, and for such longer period as any examination, inquiry, or proceeding may require. Records are
maintained in a form that permits accurate reproduction, whether the original was created on paper or electronically, and a reproduction is treated as an original
for all ordinary purposes.

You are encouraged to keep your own permanent file containing the note, the security instrument, the closing disclosures, each annual escrow analysis and
interest statement, and evidence of your insurance and tax payments. Documents of that kind are frequently needed years later in connection with a refinance,
a tax question, an insurance claim, or the sale of the property at 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345, and reconstructing them after the fact can be slow and
may involve a research fee.

7.0 Paying Extra Toward Principal
You may pay more than the amount due at any time. To ensure that the extra amount is applied to principal rather than held for the next installment, indicate
the additional principal amount on the coupon or in the designated field of the online payment screen, or include a written instruction identifying the amount and
referencing loan number 1234567890. An unmarked overpayment may be held toward the next scheduled installment.

An additional principal payment reduces the outstanding balance and the total interest paid over the life of the loan, but it does not change the amount or the
due date of the next scheduled payment unless your note expressly provides otherwise. Continue to make each regular monthly payment in full after making
an additional principal payment.

8.0 Suspense Balances and Payoff
When the loan is paid in full, any amount remaining in suspense is applied to the payoff or refunded to you, and the payoff statement identifies how a suspense
balance is being treated. A suspense balance is not automatically deducted from the payoff figure quoted to a third party, so the settlement agent should
confirm the treatment before disbursing funds.

If servicing is transferred, funds held in suspense transfer with the loan and continue to be held under the same terms by the transferee servicer. The transfer
notice furnished to you identifies the date after which payments should be sent to the new servicer.

9.0 Effect of a Transfer of Servicing
The servicing of loan number 1234567890 — the collection of payments, the administration of any escrow account, and the handling of your inquiries — may
be transferred to another company at any time. A transfer of servicing is not a sale of your obligation to a different borrower and does not change the interest
rate, the payment amount, the maturity date, or any other term of the note or the security instrument.

Where servicing transfers, you receive a notice from the transferor at least fifteen (15) days before the effective date and a notice from the transferee within
fifteen (15) days after it, unless the transfer occurs in circumstances for which the law permits a combined or later notice. The notices identify both companies,
the date payments should begin going to the new servicer, and the telephone numbers at which each may be reached.

For sixty (60) days after the effective date of a transfer, a payment received by the prior servicer on or before its due date may not be treated as late merely
because it was sent to the wrong company. Even so, redirect your payments promptly, and update any automatic payment arrangement you maintain through
your own financial institution, since that arrangement is under your control rather than ours.

10.0 Protecting Yourself Against Fraud
Mortgage transactions attract fraud, most commonly in the form of messages that appear to come from a lender, a settlement agent, or a real estate
professional and that direct funds to an account controlled by a criminal. We do not transmit wiring instructions by electronic message, and we do not change
previously issued remittance instructions by electronic message. Verify any such instruction by telephone at a number you have independently confirmed
before transferring funds.

Report a suspicious communication concerning loan number 1234567890 to us at (555) 555-0120 promptly, and preserve the message rather than deleting it.
If funds have already been transmitted, contact your financial institution immediately and ask that a recall be initiated; the prospects of recovery diminish
sharply within hours, and prompt action is by far the most important factor.

11.0 Questions About Payment Application
If you believe a payment was misapplied, held in suspense in error, or credited on an incorrect date, contact the servicer at (555) 555-0120 or submit a written
notice of error to 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY 12345. A written notice invokes the error-resolution procedures described in the separate notice furnished to
you, which require an acknowledgment and a substantive response within defined periods.

This policy is provided as of November 14, 2024 and applies to loan number 1234567890 until superseded. It summarizes the payment terms of your loan
documents; in the event of a conflict, the note, the security instrument, and the partial payment entry on your Closing Disclosure control.

12.0 Credit Reporting
We may furnish information about the status and payment history of loan number 1234567890 to one or more consumer reporting agencies, and we do so in
accordance with the accuracy and dispute-handling requirements that federal law imposes on furnishers. Information furnished ordinarily includes the account
type, the date opened, the balance, the scheduled payment, and the payment status as of the reporting date.

13.0 Complaint Procedures
If you are dissatisfied with any aspect of the handling of loan number 1234567890, we ask that you first raise the matter with us by telephone at (555)
555-0120 or in writing at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY 12345, describing the issue, the dates and amounts involved, and the resolution you seek. Most

You may also, at any time and without first contacting us, submit a complaint to the federal consumer complaint system, to the state regulator having
jurisdiction over the institution in NY, or to the federal banking agency that supervises us. Raising a concern with us does not waive, shorten, or otherwise limit
any right you have to pursue the matter with a regulator or through any other remedy available at law or in equity.

14.0 Compliance With Applicable Law
This document and the transaction it concerns are subject to the federal statutes and regulations governing residential mortgage credit and to the law of the
State of NY. Where federal law preempts or supplements state law as to a particular matter, federal law controls as to that matter; where state law affords you a
greater protection that is not preempted, that protection applies.

If a change in law or regulation requires a provision of this document to be modified, the provision is deemed amended to the minimum extent necessary to
bring it into compliance, and the remainder continues in effect. No provision should be construed to require any act that applicable law prohibits, or to prohibit
any act that applicable law requires.

15.0 Automatic Payment Arrangements
Where you authorize an automatic monthly debit, the amount debited is the total then due, and it changes when your escrow analysis changes the payment.
Confirm the amount of the first debit after any analysis so that the change is expected. You may cancel or modify the authorization by notifying us within the
period stated in the authorization, generally at least three business days before the scheduled date.

An arrangement you establish through your own bank's bill-payment service is under your control rather than ours; we can neither change nor cancel it. If the
payment amount changes, update that arrangement yourself, because a bill-payment service continues to send the former amount indefinitely, producing a
small shortfall each month that eventually accumulates into a missed installment.

16.0 Accessibility Assistance
We endeavor to make our communications accessible. If you require this or any other document in an alternative format, including large print, or if you need
assistance in reading or completing any document relating to loan number 1234567890, contact us at (555) 555-0120 and we will make reasonable
arrangements at no charge to you.

A request for an alternative format has no effect on the evaluation of an application, on the terms available to you, or on the servicing of your account, and no
record of such a request is used for any purpose other than fulfilling it. If you use an assistive technology that has difficulty with a document we have provided,
we welcome that information so that our materials may be improved.

17.0 Payments From Third Parties
We may accept a payment tendered by a person other than a borrower, such as a family member or a settlement agent, and acceptance of such a payment
does not make that person liable on the loan, does not confer any right to information about the account, and does not create any relationship between that
person and ABC Mortgage Company beyond the transaction itself.

Information about loan number 1234567890 is released only to a borrower or to a person you have authorized in writing. A third party who remits a payment
and then wishes to confirm its application must be authorized by you, and we will explain the authorization process to that person without disclosing account
information in the meantime.

18.0 Biweekly and Accelerated Payment Plans
Some borrowers arrange to pay half of a monthly payment every two weeks, which produces one additional monthly payment each year and shortens the term.
Where we offer such a plan, its terms, including when funds are applied and whether a fee applies, are stated in the plan agreement. Funds under such a plan
are ordinarily held until a full contractual payment is available and then applied.

The same result can be achieved without a plan and without a fee by adding an amount equal to one-twelfth of a monthly payment to each regular payment
and designating it as additional principal. Third-party services that offer to administer accelerated payments for a fee provide no benefit that you cannot obtain
directly, and they insert an intermediary between you and the servicer.

ABC MORTGAGE COMPANY — NMLS LICENSING AND IDENTIFICATION DISCLOSURE
Loan #1234567890 · ABC Mortgage Company · 11/24/2024
Form No. MTG-1274 · Edition 3.6 · Issued 07/18/2024



This notice is provided to John Doe by ABC Mortgage Company in connection with loan number 1234567890 and describes the licensing, registration,
and identification requirements applicable to the individuals and entities that originate residential mortgage loans. Federal law requires that every
residential mortgage loan originator be either licensed under the law of the state in which the origination occurs or registered with the Nationwide
Multistate Licensing System and Registry, and that the unique identifier assigned to the originator and to the sponsoring institution appear on specified
loan documents. This notice explains what those identifiers mean, how you may verify them, and what standards of conduct apply to the individual
assisting you as of November 14, 2024. Terms used but not defined in this document have the meanings given to them in your loan documents.

Section 1. Licensing and Registration Requirement
The Secure and Fair Enforcement for Mortgage Licensing Act establishes a national framework for the supervision of residential mortgage loan originators. An
individual who takes a residential mortgage loan application, or who offers or negotiates the terms of a residential mortgage loan for compensation or gain,
must be licensed by the appropriate NY regulator or, if employed by a federally insured depository institution or its subsidiary, registered with the Registry.
Licensing entails testing, pre-licensure and continuing education, a criminal-background review, a credit review, and the posting of a surety bond or its
equivalent.

Both the sponsoring institution and the individual originator are assigned a unique identifier by the Registry. That identifier stays with the individual across
employers and across states, which allows a consumer to trace an originator's employment and disciplinary history over the course of a career. ABC Mortgage
Company maintains the licensure and registration status of each individual authorized to originate loans on its behalf and does not permit an unlicensed or
unregistered person to perform origination activity.

Section 2. Where the Identifiers Appear
The unique identifier of the individual originator who assisted you and that of ABC Mortgage Company appear on your loan application, on the Loan Estimate
and Closing Disclosure, and on the note, in the fields designated for that purpose. The identifiers are also included in advertising, on business cards, and in
electronic correspondence relating to your transaction. If you receive a document relating to loan number 1234567890 that omits an identifier where one is
required, you may request that a corrected copy be furnished to you.

The identifier is a licensing reference number only. It is not an account number, it conveys no authority to access your loan, and it does not by itself indicate that
any particular individual is authorized to receive payment from you. Payments and payoff funds should be directed only to the addresses and accounts
identified in your payment coupon, billing statement, or written payoff statement.

Section 3. Standards of Conduct
A licensed or registered originator is prohibited from employing any scheme or device to defraud or mislead a borrower, from engaging in unfair or deceptive
practices, from obtaining property by fraud or misrepresentation, and from soliciting or entering into a contract in which the compensation is contingent upon a
specified appraised value. An originator may not make, in any manner, a false or deceptive statement concerning the rates, points, or other financing terms
available to a consumer.

Originators are further prohibited from negligently making a false statement or knowingly omitting a material fact in connection with information provided to a
federal or state regulator. ABC Mortgage Company maintains written policies, periodic training, and supervisory review designed to ensure that the individuals
acting on its behalf observe these standards throughout the origination of loan number 1234567890.

Section 4. Transfer of the Loan
We may sell, assign, transfer, pledge, or otherwise convey the loan, the loan documents, or the right to service the loan, in whole or in part, at any time and
without your consent, except as applicable law requires. A transfer of ownership or of servicing does not by itself change the interest rate, the payment amount,
the maturity date, or any other term of your obligation, and the transferee succeeds to the rights and, to the extent of the transfer, the obligations described in
the loan documents.

This document binds and benefits you and us and our respective heirs, executors, administrators, successors, and permitted assigns. You may not assign or
delegate your rights or obligations without our prior written consent, and the sale or transfer of the property at 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345 does not
release you from liability for the debt unless we expressly agree in writing to a release.

Section 5. Loan Originator Compensation
Federal law prohibits compensating a loan originator on the basis of the terms of a transaction, including the interest rate, the presence or absence of a
prepayment penalty, or any proxy for such a term. Compensation may be based on the amount of credit extended, on the number of transactions closed, on
the quality of the files produced, or on similar permissible factors. This restriction is designed to remove any financial incentive for an originator to steer you
toward terms less favorable than those for which you qualify.

An originator may not receive compensation from both you and another person in connection with the same transaction. Where you pay the originator directly,
no compensation may be received from the creditor or any other party, and where the creditor pays, no additional origination compensation may be collected
from you. The compensation arrangement applicable to your transaction is reflected in the origination charges disclosed on your Loan Estimate and Closing
Disclosure.

Section 6. Third-Party Service Providers
We engage third parties to perform functions in connection with the origination and servicing of residential mortgage loans, including document preparation,
data processing, payment processing, tax and flood determination services, insurance tracking, appraisal management, printing, and mailing. Those providers
receive only the information necessary to perform the service for which they are engaged.

Each provider is bound by contract to maintain the confidentiality and security of the information disclosed to it and to use that information only for the purposes
of the engagement. Engaging a service provider does not relieve us of responsibility for the performance of the function delegated, and inquiries concerning
any such function may be directed to us rather than to the provider.

Section 7. Telephone Communications and Call Monitoring
Telephone calls between you and ABC Mortgage Company may be monitored or recorded for quality assurance, training, and recordkeeping purposes, and
you consent to that monitoring and recording by continuing with a call after being advised of it. Recordings are retained in accordance with our records
schedule and are used only for the purposes described here and as applicable law otherwise permits or requires.

By providing a telephone number in connection with this transaction, you agree that we, our affiliates, our agents, and our service providers may contact you at
that number regarding the account, including by using an automatic dialing system or a prerecorded or artificial voice, and by text message, to the extent
permitted by applicable law. Message and data rates charged by your carrier may apply to any text message you receive.

You may withdraw consent to be contacted at a particular number, or ask that we use a different number or another method entirely, by notifying us at (555)
555-0120 or in writing at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY 12345. Withdrawing consent for automated calls does not prevent us from delivering the notices that
law requires, which may still be sent by mail or by another permitted method.

Section 8. Anti-Steering Requirements
You may not be steered to a transaction on the basis of the compensation the originator would receive when you qualify for a different transaction on more
favorable terms. Where multiple loan options are presented, the originator is expected to present options that include the lowest interest rate for which you
qualify, the lowest rate without risky features such as negative amortization or a balloon payment in the first seven years, and the lowest total dollar amount of
discount points and origination fees.

If you were presented with more than one financing option in connection with the property at 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345, the comparison provided
to you at the time is retained in the loan file. You may request a copy of that comparison at any time during the origination of the loan by contacting the office
identified at the end of this notice.

Section 9. Joint Borrowers and Multiple Obligors
Where more than one person is obligated on loan number 1234567890, each of you is jointly and severally liable for the entire obligation. That means the full
amount may be enforced against any one of you, against some of you, or against all of you together, without any requirement that other obligors, guarantors, or
collateral be pursued first, and a release or accommodation extended to one of you does not impair the liability of the others.

Any communication we deliver to one of you is treated as delivered to all of you, and an instruction, election, or authorization given by one of you may be acted
upon as though given by all of you unless the loan documents or applicable law require otherwise. Where your instructions conflict, we may decline to act until
the conflict is resolved among you in writing.

A change in the relationship among obligors — including a separation, a divorce, a transfer of an interest in the property, or the death of a borrower — does not
by itself alter the obligation or release any person from it. Notify us of such an event so that our records reflect the correct parties, and consult your own
attorney concerning the effect of the event on the ownership of 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345.

Section 10. Compliance With Applicable Law
This document and the transaction it concerns are subject to the federal statutes and regulations governing residential mortgage credit and to the law of the
State of NY. Where federal law preempts or supplements state law as to a particular matter, federal law controls as to that matter; where state law affords you a
greater protection that is not preempted, that protection applies.

If a change in law or regulation requires a provision of this document to be modified, the provision is deemed amended to the minimum extent necessary to
bring it into compliance, and the remainder continues in effect. No provision should be construed to require any act that applicable law prohibits, or to prohibit
any act that applicable law requires.

Section 11. Keeping Your Information Current
Notify us promptly of any change in your mailing address, telephone number, or electronic address, and of any change in the name in which the account is
held. Until we have received notice of a change and have had a reasonable opportunity to act upon it, we are entitled to rely on the information most recently
reflected in our records, and a communication sent to that information remains effective.

Keeping your information current matters most at exactly the moments it is easiest to overlook: after a move, after a change in marital status, after a change in
electronic mail provider, and after the transfer of servicing. Several of the notices described in the documents furnished to you carry response deadlines, and a
notice that does not reach you still starts the period it establishes.

Section 12. Employment and Supervision
Each individual originating loans for ABC Mortgage Company does so under the sponsorship and supervision of the institution, whose own license or
registration authorizes the activity in the jurisdictions where it operates. Sponsorship must be active and reflected in the Registry at the time an application is
taken; an originator whose sponsorship has lapsed may not take an application or negotiate terms until the sponsorship is reinstated.

Independent contractors, third-party processors, and administrative personnel who do not take applications or negotiate terms are not required to be licensed
as originators, but they remain subject to the confidentiality, information-security, and fair-lending obligations that govern the handling of your file. ABC
Mortgage Company remains responsible for the conduct of the persons to whom it delegates any function relating to loan number 1234567890.

Section 13. Complaints and Regulatory Contacts
If you believe that an individual or entity involved in your transaction has acted improperly, you may file a complaint with the NY regulator that issued the
applicable license, with the Registry, or with the federal agency having jurisdiction over the institution. Complaints may generally be submitted online, by mail,
or by telephone, and the regulator will advise you of the information required to open a file.

You are also invited to bring the matter to our attention first by writing to ABC Mortgage Company at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY 12345 or calling (555)
555-0120. Raising a concern with us does not waive, shorten, or otherwise limit any right you have to pursue the matter with a regulator or through any other
remedy available under federal or NY law.

Section 14. Effect of This Notice
This notice is informational. It does not create any contractual right, does not constitute a commitment to extend credit, and does not modify the terms of the
note, the security instrument, or any disclosure furnished to you in connection with loan number 1234567890. The licensing framework described here exists
independently of your loan and continues to apply to the individuals involved regardless of whether your transaction closes.

Retain this notice with your loan records. If your loan is later sold or its servicing transferred, the licensing identifiers applicable to the new holder or servicer will
be furnished to you by that party in its own communications, and the identifiers shown on the documents you signed at closing will remain accurate as of
November 14, 2024 for the origination of this transaction.

Section 15. Continuing Education and Testing
A licensed originator must pass a qualified written examination covering federal law and regulation, state law relating to mortgage origination, and ethical and
fraud-prevention topics, and must complete pre-licensure education before the license is issued. Continuing education is required each year in order to renew,
and a license that is not renewed within the annual window lapses.

Registered originators employed by federally insured depository institutions are not subject to the same testing and education requirements, but they are
subject to background screening, to registration in the Registry, and to the supervision of the institution and its federal regulator. Both channels are subject to
the standards of conduct described in this notice.

Section 16. Records of Your Transaction
The identity of the individual who took your application, of any processor or underwriter who worked on the file, and of the persons who communicated with you
is recorded in the loan file for loan number 1234567890, together with the dates and substance of material communications. Those records are retained for the
periods that applicable law prescribes.

If a question later arises about what was represented to you during origination, that record is the starting point for resolving it. Keeping your own notes of
significant conversations, including dates, names, and what was said, is a simple habit that makes any later inquiry easier for both of us to answer accurately.

          Notice Concerning   Property Taxes  and  Hazard  Insurance
          ABC MORTGAGE COMPANY — NOTICE CONCERNING PROPERTY TAXES AND HAZARD INSURANCE — PLEASE READ AND RETAIN
          Loan #1234567890 - ABC Mortgage Company - 11/29/2024
          Document LN-1411 - Rev. 4.9 - In effect as of 06/11/2024
                                                                                             ee
          Where this document summarizes the law, the law itself controls in the event of any difference. This notice summarizes the obligations of John Doe with
          respect to property taxes, assessments, and insurance coverage on the property located at 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345, which secures loan
          number 1234567890, These obligations continue for the entire term of the loan and exist whether or not an escrow account is maintained. They arise
          from the security instrument you sign at closing and from the law of NY, and a failure to meet them can result in a lien with priority over the mortgage, in
          an uninsured loss, or in charges assessed to your account. The notice is provided as of November 14, 2024 for your reference.
          Article |. Real Estate Taxes
          General real estate taxes are assessed by the county or municipality in which the property lies and are billed on a cycle established by local law. Unpaid taxes
          become a lien on the property that generally takes priority over the mortgage, and continued nonpayment can result in a tax sale of the property or of the tax
          lien itself, in either case on a timetable set by statute rather than by the lender.
         Where an escrow account is maintained, the servicer pays the general tax bill from escrow. You should nonetheless review each assessment notice and tax bill
          you receive to confirm that the assessed value, the exemptions applied, and the parcel identification are correct. An error in any of those items affects the
         amount escrowed and is corrected through the assessor, not through the servicer.
         Article ll. Required Hazard Insurance
         The security instrument requires that the improvements be insured against loss by fire, hazards within the term "extended coverage,” and other hazards for
         which insurance is required, in the amounts and for the periods required, with a carrier acceptable to the lender. The policy must name the lender and its
         successors and assigns as mortgagee so that notice of cancellation is received and the lender's interest is protected.
         Coverage must be maintained continuously. A policy cancelled for nonpayment, not renewed at expiration, or reduced below the required amount leaves the
         collateral unprotected and permits the servicer to place coverage at your expense after the notices described in the separate lender-placed insurance notice.
         Confirm at each renewal that the mortgagee clause names the current servicer at the current address.
         Article Ill. Flood and Other Specialized Coverage
         Where the property is located in a special flood hazard area, flood insurance is required by federal law for the term of the loan, in an amount at least equal to
         the lesser of the outstanding principal balance, the insurable value of the improvements, or the maximum available under the National Flood Insurance
         Program. The determination applicable to your property is disclosed to you separately.
         Depending on the location and characteristics of the property, other coverage may be required or advisable, including windstorm or named-storm coverage in
         coastal areas, earthquake coverage where the exposure warrants it, and a walls-in policy where a condominium or homeowners association maintains a
         master policy. Review the association's coverage where applicable to confirm what it does and does not insure.
         Article lV. Property Address and Occupancy of Record
         Our records identify the property securing loan number 1234567890 as 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345, and they reflect the occupancy status certified
         in your application. Certain program requirements, insurance obligations, and tax treatments depend upon that status, and it is therefore recorded as of the
         date of the transaction and carried forward until we are notified of a change.
         Notify us if the mailing address at which you wish to receive correspondence differs from the property address, and notify us again if either changes. A mailing
         address that differs from the property address is common and is recorded without any effect on the terms of the loan: what matters is that both are accurate so
         that notices and bills reach the right place.
         Where a change in the use or occupancy of the property is contemplated, review the security instrument and any rider attached to it, since some contain
         provisions concerning occupancy, leasing, or transfer of the property. Consult your own adviser concerning the effect of a contemplated change before it is
         made.
         Article V. Adequacy of Coverage
         The dwelling limit should be sufficient to rebuild the structure at current construction costs, which may differ substantially from the purchase price or the
         assessed value. Review the limit annually, and consider whether an extended or guaranteed replacement cost endorsement is appropriate. Review the
         deductible as well, particularly any percentage deductible applicable to wind, hail, or named storms.
         Consider also whether your personal property limits, loss-of-use coverage, and liability limits are adequate for your circumstances. Those coverages protect
         you rather than the lender and are not addressed by the minimum requirements of the security instrument. An insurance professional can evaluate the
         adequacy of coverage on 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345.
         Article VI. Identity Verification Requirements
         Federal law requires all financial institutions to obtain, verify, and record information identifying each person who opens an account, in order to help the
         government fight the funding of terrorism and money-laundering activities. When you apply for credit, we ask for your name, address, date of birth, and other
         information that allows us to identify you, and we may ask to see a driver's license or other identifying document.
                                               Retain this document with your loan file records.        Page 1 of 3
        The information collected for this purpose is used to verify identity and is retained in accordance with applicable law. It is not used as a factor in evaluating
         creditworthiness, and requesting identifying documentation is a routine step applied to every applicant rather than an indication of any concern about a
        particular transaction.
        Article Vil. Credit Reporting
         We may furnish information about the status and payment history of loan number 1234567890 to one or more consumer reporting agencies, and we do so in
        accordance with the accuracy and dispute-handling requirements that federal law imposes on furnishers. Information furnished ordinarily includes the account
        type, the date opened, the balance, the scheduled payment, and the payment status as of the reporting date.
        If you believe that information we have furnished about this account is inaccura te or incomplete, you may notify us in writing at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY
         12345, describi ng the item and the reason you believe it to be incorrect and enclosing any supporting documentation. We will investigate, report the results to
        you, and correct any inaccuracy with each agency to which the information was furnished.
         You may also dispute the item directly with the consumer reporting agency, which must generally conduct its own reasonable reinvestigation. Disputing with us
        and with the agency are independent routes and may be used together; neither route requires payment of any fee, and no service can lawfully remove
         information that is accurate and current.
         Article Vill. Compliance With Applicable Law
        This document and the transaction it concerns are subject to the federal statutes and regulations governing residential mortgage credit and to the law of the
        State of NY. Where federal law preempts or supplements state law as to a particu! lar matter, federal law controls as to that matter; where state law affords you a
        greater protection that is not preempted, that protection applies.
        If a change in law or regulation requires a provision of this document to be modified, the provision is deemed amended to the minimum extent necessary to
        bring it into compliance, and the remainder continues in effect. No provision should be construed to require any act that applicable law prohibits, or to prohibit
         any act that applicable law requires.
        Article IX. Relationship to Your Other Loan Documents
        This document supplements the note, the security instrument, and the disclosures furnished to you in connection with loan number 1234567890. It does not
        enlarge, reduce, or otherwise modify the amounts payable, the interest rate, the payment schedule, or any right or remedy established by those instruments,
        and no statement here should be read as a representation that any particular term applies to your transaction .
        Where this document summarizes a statute, a regulation, or a program requirement, the summary is provided for convenience, In the event of any difference
        between the summary and the authority summarized, the statute, regulation, or program requirement controls, and no summary in this document limits any

       Article XI. Claims and Loss Proceeds
        Report a loss to your carrier promptly and notify the servicer, because the security instrument gives the lender an interest in insurance proceeds. Where a loss
        is significant, proceeds are commonly issued jointly to you and to the servicer and are disbursed against the progress of repairs under a loss-draft process that
        requires documentation such as the adjusters report, contractor estimates, and inspections.
       The purpose of that process is to ensure that proceeds are used to restore the collateral. It is administered under the terms of the security instrument and
       applicable law. Contact the servicer as soon as a loss occurs so that the requirements are understood before repairs begin and so that disbursements are not
       delayed by missing documentation.

        Article Xill. Association Dues and Other Charges
        Where the property is subject to a homeowners or condominium association, the assessments levied by that association are your direct responsibility and are
        ordinarily not escrowed. Unpaid assessments can become a lien on the property under NY law, and in some jurisdictions a portion of that lien has priority over
        the mortgage. Utility charges, in certain jurisdictions, may likewise become a lien if unpaid.
        Keep association assessments and utility obligations current, and retain evidence of payment. If an association changes its billing address or management
       company, update your records promptly so that invoices continue to reach you.
        Article XIV. If Taxes or Premiums Go Unpaid
        Where an obligation on the property goes unpaid, the security instrument permits the lender to advance the funds necessary to protect its interest, including
        paying delinquent taxes or purchasing insurance coverage, and to recover the advance from you together with interest at the rate provided in the loan
        documents. An advance of that kind is added to the amount you owe.
        An advance is a remedy of last resort rather than a service, and it is materially more expensive than paying the obligation yourself. Where an escrow account
        exists, advances are rare because the servicer pays the escrowed items directly; where no escrow account exists, the responsibility to monitor and pay each
         bill rests entirely with you.
         Article XV. No Professional Advice Provided
         This document is furnished for informational purposes and summarizes requirements, policies, or procedures in general terms. It does not constitute legal, tax,
         accounting, insurance, or investment advice, and neither ABC Mortgage Company nor any of its employees or agents is acting as your adviser in any of those
         capacities. Statements made here are necessarily general and may not address the particular facts of your situation.
         You should consult your own attorney, tax adviser, insurance professional, or financial adviser regarding the application of the matters described here to your
         circumstances, including the deductibility of interest and taxes, the adequacy of insurance coverage on the property, and the effect of the transaction on your
         estate or financial planning. The cost of such advice is modest relative to the size of a residential mortgage obligation.
         Article XVI. Year-End Tax Information
         Following each calendar year, the servicer furnishes a statement of the mortgage interest you paid, together with information about points and, where the
         servicer disbursed them, real estate taxes paid from escrow. The statement is furnished by the deadline the Internal Revenue Service prescribes and is also
         reported to that agency.
         The deductibility of mortgage interest and property taxes depends on your individual circumstances and on limits established by tax law. The servicer reports
         amounts; it does not advise on deductibility. Consult your own tax adviser regarding the treatment of the amounts shown on the statement for the property at
         456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345.
         Article XVII. If the Property Is Damaged
         Report damage to your insurance carrier promptly, document the condition with photographs before repairs begin, and retain every estimate, invoice, and
         receipt. Notify the servicer as well, because the security instrument gives the lender an interest in the proceeds and, for a significant loss, a loss-draft process
         governs how funds are released.
          Continue making your monthly payments while a claim is pending. A casualty does not suspend the obligation to pay, and the two matters are handled on
          separate tracks; allowing the loan to fall behind while a claim is processed creates a second problem without resolving the first.

HMDA Data Collection Notice
IMPORTANT NOTICE — HMDA DATA COLLECTION NOTICE
Loan #1234567890 · ABC Mortgage Company · 12/04/2024
Form MTG-1548 · Rev. 5.2 · Effective 05/05/2024



You may request an additional copy of this document at any time at no charge. The Home Mortgage Disclosure Act requires certain financial institutions,
including ABC Mortgage Company, to collect and report information about applications for, and originations and purchases of, home mortgage loans.
This notice is furnished to John Doe in connection with loan number 1234567890 and the property located at 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345. It
explains what information is collected, why the law requires it, how the information is disclosed to the public, and the limits that apply to its use. The data
reported under this statute play no part in the evaluation of your creditworthiness and cannot lawfully be used as a basis for any decision concerning
your application.

1.0 Purpose of the Statute
The Home Mortgage Disclosure Act was enacted to provide the public and public officials with sufficient information to determine whether financial institutions
are serving the housing needs of the communities in which they are located, to assist public officials in distributing public-sector investment so as to attract
private investment where it is most needed, and to assist in identifying possible discriminatory lending patterns and enforcing anti-discrimination statutes. The
statute is a disclosure and monitoring law; it does not direct any institution to make any particular loan.

The data collected under the statute are used by regulators, researchers, community organizations, and the public to examine lending patterns across
geographies, loan products, and applicant characteristics. Because the analysis depends upon complete and accurate reporting, ABC Mortgage Company
maintains procedures designed to ensure that the information recorded for each application, including the application associated with loan number
1234567890, is collected consistently and reported without alteration.

2.0 Complaints and Escalation
If you are dissatisfied with any aspect of the handling of loan number 1234567890, we ask that you first raise the matter with us by telephone at (555)
555-0120 or in writing at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY 12345, describing the issue, the dates and amounts involved, and the resolution you seek. Most
concerns are resolved fastest at that level, and a written summary from you is the most reliable way to ensure the matter is understood as you intend it.

You may also, at any time and without first contacting us, submit a complaint to the federal consumer complaint system, to the state regulator having
jurisdiction over the institution in NY, or to the federal banking agency that supervises us. Raising a concern with us does not waive, shorten, or otherwise limit
any right you have to pursue the matter with a regulator or through any other remedy available at law or in equity.

3.0 Communication Preferences
You may tell us how you prefer to be reached, and we will honor a stated preference where the nature of the communication and applicable law permit. Certain
communications must be delivered in a specific manner regardless of preference, and those are sent by the required method even where you have asked to be
contacted only in another way.

Marketing communications are distinct from servicing communications. You may opt out of marketing by contacting us at (555) 555-0120 or by following the
instructions contained in the communication itself, and doing so does not affect the delivery of statements, disclosures, escrow analyses, or any other
communication concerning the administration of loan number 1234567890.

Where you have asked to receive communications electronically, keep the electronic address on file current and add our sending address to the list of
permitted senders in your mail application, so that a notice is not diverted to a junk folder. A notice diverted in that manner remains effective as of the date it
was sent.

4.0 Effect of a Transfer of Servicing
The servicing of loan number 1234567890 — the collection of payments, the administration of any escrow account, and the handling of your inquiries — may
be transferred to another company at any time. A transfer of servicing is not a sale of your obligation to a different borrower and does not change the interest
rate, the payment amount, the maturity date, or any other term of the note or the security instrument.

Where servicing transfers, you receive a notice from the transferor at least fifteen (15) days before the effective date and a notice from the transferee within
fifteen (15) days after it, unless the transfer occurs in circumstances for which the law permits a combined or later notice. The notices identify both companies,
the date payments should begin going to the new servicer, and the telephone numbers at which each may be reached.

For sixty (60) days after the effective date of a transfer, a payment received by the prior servicer on or before its due date may not be treated as late merely
because it was sent to the wrong company. Even so, redirect your payments promptly, and update any automatic payment arrangement you maintain through
your own financial institution, since that arrangement is under your control rather than ours.

5.0 Definitions Used in This Document
Unless the context plainly requires otherwise, "you" and "your" refer to John Doe and to any other person obligated on loan number 1234567890; "we," "us,"
and "our" refer to ABC Mortgage Company and to any successor, assignee, or servicer that acquires the loan or the right to service it; and "the property" refers
to the real property located at 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345 that secures the loan. "Applicable law" means the federal statutes and regulations
governing residential mortgage credit together with the law of the State of NY, in each case as amended from time to time.

You authorize ABC Mortgage Company, and any assignee or servicer of loan number 1234567890, to verify the information you have provided in connection

Verification may occur at any time during the origination of the credit and again before closing, and information obtained through verification is used in
evaluating the credit request and in servicing the account thereafter. Information collected in this manner is handled in accordance with the privacy notice
furnished to you and with applicable federal and NY law.

7.0 Information Collected
The information reported includes the type and purpose of the loan, the amount of credit requested, the property type, the occupancy status, the census tract
and other geographic identifiers of the property, the action taken on the application and the date of that action, and, where applicable, the reasons for denial.
Loan-level pricing and underwriting fields, including the interest rate, the total loan costs, the loan term, and certain ratios relied upon in the credit decision, are
also reported.

In addition, the statute directs the collection of the ethnicity, race, sex, and age of the applicant and, where present, the co-applicant. This demographic
information is requested solely so that regulators may monitor compliance with fair-lending law. It is recorded separately from the underwriting analysis and is
not disclosed to the personnel responsible for the credit decision except where operational constraints make separation impracticable, in which case those
personnel are instructed not to consider it.

8.0 Voluntary Nature of Demographic Information
You are not required to furnish the requested demographic information. Federal regulation provides that you may decline to provide some or all of it, and your
decision will have no effect on the processing of your application, on the terms offered to you, or on any other aspect of your relationship with ABC Mortgage
Company. If you decline, and the application is taken in person, we are required to note the information on the basis of visual observation or surname.

Where an application is taken by mail, by telephone, or over the internet and you decline to provide the information, we record that you declined and do not
supply the information ourselves. In no circumstance may your decision to provide or withhold demographic information be considered as a factor in the
disposition of the credit request associated with loan number 1234567890.

9.0 Privacy Protections
Federal regulation requires an assessment of whether the release of any particular data field would create a risk to applicant privacy that is not justified by the
benefit of disclosure. Fields that present such a risk are excluded from the public data or are transformed before release. ABC Mortgage Company does not
publish loan-level data of its own accord and discloses reported information only through the channels the statute prescribes.

Internally, information collected for reporting purposes is protected by the same physical, electronic, and procedural safeguards that apply to the rest of your
file, and access is restricted to personnel with a legitimate business need. The privacy notice furnished to you separately describes those safeguards in greater
detail and applies to demographic information in the same manner as to any other category of personal information.

10.0 This Document Is Not Advice
This document is furnished for informational purposes and summarizes requirements, policies, or procedures in general terms. It does not constitute legal, tax,
accounting, insurance, or investment advice, and neither ABC Mortgage Company nor any of its employees or agents is acting as your adviser in any of those
capacities. Statements made here are necessarily general and may not address the particular facts of your situation.

You should consult your own attorney, tax adviser, insurance professional, or financial adviser regarding the application of the matters described here to your
circumstances, including the deductibility of interest and taxes, the adequacy of insurance coverage on the property, and the effect of the transaction on your
estate or financial planning. The cost of such advice is modest relative to the size of a residential mortgage obligation.

11.0 Use in Fair-Lending Examination
Regulators use reported data as a screening tool. A statistical disparity identified in the data does not by itself establish that any institution has engaged in
unlawful conduct, because the public data set does not contain every factor that legitimately bears upon a credit decision. Where a disparity appears,
examiners obtain the underlying files and evaluate the actual basis on which each decision was made.

ABC Mortgage Company conducts periodic internal review of its own reported data for the same purpose, and it maintains a fair-lending program comprising
written policy, training, monitoring, and corrective action. Nothing in this notice limits your right to raise a fair-lending concern with us or with a regulator, or to
pursue any remedy available under the Equal Credit Opportunity Act, the Fair Housing Act, or the law of NY.

14.0 Who Must Report
Reporting obligations depend upon the type of institution, its asset size, its location, and the volume of covered loans it originates. Depository institutions
meeting an asset threshold and originating a defined number of covered closed-end mortgages or open-end lines of credit in each of the two preceding
calendar years are covered, as are non-depository institutions meeting the applicable volume thresholds.

Because the thresholds change over time and are adjusted for inflation and by rulemaking, an institution may become a reporter or cease to be one from year
to year. Where ABC Mortgage Company is a covered institution for the year in which action is taken on your application, the data described in this notice are
collected and reported; the notice is furnished in either event as a matter of routine practice.

15.0 Covered and Excluded Transactions
Covered transactions generally include applications for, originations of, and purchases of closed-end mortgage loans and open-end lines of credit secured by a
dwelling, whether the purpose is purchase, refinancing, home improvement, or another purpose. A dwelling includes a principal residence, a second home, an
investment property, a manufactured home, and a multifamily property containing five or more units.

Certain transactions are excluded from reporting, including temporary financing, loans originated in a fiduciary capacity, and transactions the regulation
specifically exempts. The classification of a transaction is determined by the regulation and not by any election of the parties, and the classification recorded for
your application reflects the characteristics of the credit you requested.

         These terms govern the use by John Doe of the online account services, mobile application, and electronic statement delivery that ABC Mortgage

          1) Signing Up
         Enrollment requires that you register an account, verify your identity by the method presented, and provide a current electronic address at which notices may
         be delivered. Only a borrower obligated on the loan, or a person you have authorized in writing, may enroll for access. Access rights are personal to the
         enrolled user and may not be transferred.
         We may decline or terminate enrollment where identity cannot be verified, where the account is not eligible for a particular service, or where use of the service
         appears inconsistent with these terms, Termination of online access does not affect the underlying loan obligation, the delivery of required notices, or any other
         right or duty of either party.
         2) Electronic Statement Delivery
         If you elect electronic delivery, your periodic statement is posted to the secure site each cycle and a notification is sent to the electronic address on file. The
         Statement is deemed delivered when posted and the notification is sent, whether or not you open it. It remains available online for the retention period
         described below, and you may download or print a copy at any time.
         Electing electronic delivery of statements does not by itself change the delivery method for other communications. Certain notices may continue to be sent on
         paper where law, investor requirement, or our own Practice so provides, and we may revert to paper delivery for any communication at our discretion or where
         an electronic notification is returned undeliverable.
         3) Your Credentials
         You are responsible for maintaining the confidentiality of your user identification, password, and any multifactor authentication device or code, and for all
        activity occurring under your credentials. Do not share credentials with any person, including a family member or a person assisting you with your finances: a
        Person who needs access should be authorized through the process we provide rather than by sharing a password.
         Notify us immediately at (555) 555-0120 if you believe your credentials have been compromised or that an unauthorized person has accessed your account.
         Prompt notice allows access to be suspended and credentials reset. We will never ask you for your full password by telephone, by electronic message, or
         through a link contained in a message.
         4) Security Practices
         Access the service by entering the address directly or by using an application obtained from an official application store, rather than by following a link
         contained in an unexpected message. Keep the operating system and browser of your device current, use a unique password for financial services, and enable
         multifactor authentication where it is offered.
         Be alert to messages that create urgency, that request credentials or payment through an unfamiliar channel, or that direct payoff or payment funds to an
        account differing from the instructions on your statement. We do not change remittance instructions by electronic message, and any such message should be
         verified by telephone at a number you have independently confirmed.
         5) Availability of Service
        The service is generally available at all times but may be interrupted for scheduled maintenance, for emergency repairs, or by circumstances beyond our
        reasonable control, including interruptions in telecommunications or utility service. We do not warrant uninterrupted or error-free Operation, and we are not
        responsible for the performance of your device, your software, or your internet connection.
        Interruption of the service does not extend a payment due date or excuse a payment obligation. Where the service is unavailable near a due date, use an
        alternative payment method described on your statement so that the payment is received on time; contact us if you require assistance in doing so.
        6) Online Payments
        A payment scheduled through the service is initiated on the date you specify, subject to the cutoff time posted on the site. Payments initiated after the cutoff, or
        on a day that is not a business day, are ordinarily processed on the next business day. You are responsible for ensuring that sufficient funds are available in the
        account you designate.
        You may cancel or modify a scheduled payment until it begins processing. A payment returned unpaid is reversed, and a returned-item fee may be assessed
        as permitted by law and by your loan documents. Recurring automatic payments continue until you cancel them, and canceling within the period the site
        specifies before the scheduled date prevents the next debit.

        Federal servicing regulations give John Doe the right to submit a written notice of asserted error and a written request for information concerning loan
        number 1234567890, and they require the servicer to acknowledge and respond within defined periods. This document identifies the exclusive address
        for such submissions, describes what a qualifying notice or request must contain, states the deadlines that apply, and explains the protections that
        attach while a submission is pending. These procedures apply for the life of the loan secured by the property at 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345
        and should be retained for future reference. Where this document summarizes the law, the law itself controls in the event of any difference.
        Section 1. Exclusive Address for Submissions
        A notice of error or a request for information must be sent in writing to the address the servicer designates for that purpose. The designated address is stated
        on your periodic statement, on the servicer’ 's website, and in the notice of transfer of servicing where servicing changes. A submission sent to any other
        address, including a payment remittance address, may not trigger the regulatory deadlines.
        Written submissions concerning loan number 1234567890 should be directed to ABC Mortgage Company at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY 12345 unless a
        different designated address has been provided to you in writing. Telephone conversations, while often the fastest way to resolve a routine question, do not
        invoke the procedures described in this document, which apply only to written submissions.
         Section 2. Computation of Time Periods
        Unless a particular statute, regulation, or provision states otherwise, a period expressed in days is measured in calendar days, the day of the act or event that
        starts the period is excluded, and the last day is included. Where the last day falls on a Saturday, a Sunday, or a legal public holiday, the period runs to the end
        of the next day that is not one of those days.
        Several requirements applicable to residential mortgage transactions are measured in business days, and the definition of a business day differs among them:
        one rule counts days on which our offices are open for substantially all business, while another counts all calendar days except Sundays and legal public
        holidays. Where a specific count controls a right or a deadline, it is stated in the provision that establishes it.
        Where a period is measured from the delivery of a document, delivery by mail is generally presumed to occur three business days after mailing unless earlier
        receipt is documented. Because these conventions determine real deadlines in your transaction, confirm the applicable dates with us or with your settlement
        agent rather than estimating them.
         Section 3. Severability of Provisions
         if any provision of this document is held by a court or other tribunal of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, that holding shall not affect
        any other provision, and the remainder shall continue in full force and effect as though the offending provision had never been included . The parties intend that
         each provision be severable and that this document be given effect to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law.
        Where a provision is unenforceable only because it exceeds a limit imposed by law, it shall be deemed reduced or reformed to the maximum extent the law
        permits and enforced as so modified, so as to give effect to the original intent to the greatest degree possible. Nothing in this document waives or limits any
         right afforded to you by a mandatory provision of federal law or of the law of NY.
         Section 4. Updating Your Contact Information
         Notify us promptly of any change in your mailing address, telephone number, or electronic address, and of any change in the name in which the account is
         held. Until we have received notice of a change and have had a reasonable opportunity to act upon it, we are entitled to rely on the information most recently
         reflected in our records, and a communication sent to that information remains effective.
         Keeping your information current matters most at exactly the moments it is easiest to overlook: after a move, after a change in marital status, after a change in
         electronic mail provider, and after the transfer of servicing. Several of the notices described in the documents furnished to you carry response deadlines, and a
         notice that does not reach you still starts the period it establishes.
         Section 5. Customer Identification Program Notice
         Federal law requires all financial institutions to obtain, verify, and record information identifying each person who opens an account, in order to help the
         government fight the funding of terrorism and money-laundering activities. . When you apply for credit, we ask for your name, address, date of birth, and other
         information that allows us to identify you, and we may ask to see a driver’ 's license or other identifying document.
         The information collected for this purpose is used to verify identity and is retained in accordance with applicable law. It is not used as a factor in evaluating
         creditworthiness, and requesting identifying documentation is a routine step applied to every applicant rather than an indication of any concern about a
         particular transaction.
         Section 6. Delivery and Receipt of Communications
         A communication we send to you is effective when mailed by first-class mail, postage prepaid, to the most recent address shown in our records, or, where you
         have consented to electronic delivery, when transmitted to the electronic address on file or posted to the secure site with notification to you. Effectiveness does
         not depend upon your having opened, retrieved, or read the communication, and a communication retumed undeliverable remains effective as of the date it
         was sent unless applicable law provides otherwise.
