         Where more than one person is obligated on loan number 1234567890, a communication delivered to any one of you is treated as delivered to all of you. A
          communication you send to us is effective when actually received at the address designated for that category of communication; correspondence sent to a
          payment remittance address or to an office not designated to receive it may be delayed and, for certain reguiated submissions, may not start the response
          period at all.
          Section 7. What a Request for Information Must Contain
          A request for information must state the name of the borrower, information that enables the servicer to identify the account, and the information sought. A
          request may seek documents such as a payment history, an escrow analysis, a copy of the note, or the identity of the owner or assignee of the loan. A request
          seeking the identity of the owner or assignee is subject to a shorter response deadline than other requests.
          A servicer is not required to respond to a request that is overbroad or unduly burdensome, to one that seeks confidential, proprietary, or privileged information,
          to one that is irrelevant to the servicing of the loan, or to one that is duplicative of a request already answered. Where a response is declined on one of those
          grounds, the servicer notifies you in writing and states the basis.
          Section 8. Legal Compliance
         This document and the transaction it concerns are subject to the federal statutes and regulations governing residential mortgage credit and to the law of the
          State of NY. Where federal law preempts or supplements state law as to a particular matter, federal law controls as to that matter; where state law affords you a
          greater protection that is not preempted, that protection applies.
          If a change in law or regulation requires a provision of this document to be modified, the provision is deemed amended to the minimum extent necessary to
          bring it into compliance, and the remainder continues in effect. No provision should be construed to require any act that applicable law prohibits, or to prohibit
          any act that applicable law requires.
          Section 9. Acknowledgment and Response Deadlines
          The servicer must acknowledge receipt of a notice of error or a request for information in writing within five (5) business days, excluding legal public holidays,
          Saturdays, and Sundays. For a notice of error, the substantive response is due within thirty (30) business days, subject to a fifteen-business-day extension in
          most cases where the servicer notifies you of the extension and the reason for it.
          Shorter deadlines apply to particular categories. An assertion that the servicer failed to provide an accurate payoff balance must be answered within seven (7)
          business days, and a request for the identity of the owner or assignee of the loan must be answered within ten (10) business days. An asserted error
          concerning a scheduled foreclosure sale must be answered before the sale or within the general period, whichever is earlier.
          Section 10. Electronic Delivery of This Document
          Where you have consented to receive records electronically, this document may be delivered to the electronic address on file or posted to a secure site with
          notification to you, and such delivery satisfies any requirement that it be provided in writing. You may withdraw that consent at any time, and you may request a
          paper copy of this or any other document delivered electronically, in each case in the manner described in the electronic records consent furnished to you.
          If you are unable to access, view, or retain a document delivered electronically, notify us at (555) 555-0120 so that a paper copy may be sent to your address of
          record. A request for a paper copy of a particular document is not, by itself, treated as a withdrawal of your consent to electronic delivery of other
          communications.
          Section 11. How the Servicer Responds
          In responding to a notice of error, the servicer must either correct the error and notify you in writing of the correction, the effective date, and the contact
          information for further assistance, or conduct a reasonable investigation and notify you in writing that no error occurred, stating the reasons and how you may
          request the documents relied upon. Those documents are provided without charge upon request.
          A response to a request for information provides the information sought and contact information for further assistance, or explains that the information is not
          available, states why, and identifies the contact for follow-up. Responses are sent to the address of record unless you designate another address in your
          submission.
          Section 12. Complaints and Escalation
          If you are dissatisfied with any aspect of the handling of loan number 1234567890, we ask that you first raise the matter with us by telephone at (555)
          555-0120 or in writing at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY 12345, describing the issue, the dates and amounts involved, and the resolution you seek. Most
          concerns are resolved fastest at that level, and a written summary from you is the most reliable way to ensure the matter is understood as you intend it.
          You may also, at any time and without first contacting us, submit a complaint to the federal consumer complaint system, to the state regulator having
          jurisdiction over the institution in NY, or to the federal banking agency that supervises us. Raising a concer with us does not waive, shorten, or otherwise limit
          any right you have to pursue the matter with a regulator or through any other remedy available at law or in equity.
          Section 13. Protections While a Submission Is Pending
          For sixty (60) days after receiving a notice of error concerning an asserted payment error, the servicer may not furnish adverse information to any consumer
          reporting agency regarding the payment that is the subject of the notice. This protection applies to the specific payment disputed and does not suspend the
          obligation to make other payments as they come due.
                                                Retain this document with your loan file records         Page 2 of
          Submitting a notice of error or a request for information does not extend a payment due date, waive a late charge properly assessed, or suspend the accrual of
          interest. It does obligate the servicer to investigate and respond, and it creates a documented record of the issue that is useful if the matter is later escalated to
          a regulator.
          Section 14. Practical Guidance for Submissions
          Submit a separate writing for each matter rather than combining several unrelated issues, state the loan number and property address at the top, describe the
          facts in chronological order, identify the specific dates and amounts involved, and enclose copies of the supporting documents. Keep a copy of everything you
          send, and send by a method that provides evidence of delivery.
         Do not include a notice of error on or with a payment coupon or check, because payment processing is automated and a notice enclosed with a remittance
         may not reach the correct department. Where the matter is urgent, a telephone call to (555) 555-0120 in addition to, rather than instead of, the written
          submission is often helpful.
          Section 15. Escalation and Other Remedies
         If you are not satisfied with the response, you may submit an additional notice identifying why the response is inadequate, and you may file a complaint with
          the federal consumer complaint system, with the NY regulator having jurisdiction over the servicer, or with the applicable federal banking agency. These
         procedures do not limit any right you have to pursue a remedy in court.
          Where a loan is transferred to a new servicer, a pending notice of error or request for information should be resubmitted to the transferee servicer at its
          designated address, because the transferor's obligation ends with respect to matters arising after the transfer date stated in the notice furnished to you.
          Section 16. Effect of These Procedures
          These procedures are provided as of November 14, 2024 and summarize the requirements of federal servicing regulation. Where this summary differs from the
          governing regulation, the regulation controls, and nothing here waives, limits, or enlarges any right you hold under federal or NY law.
          Retain this document with your loan records so that the designated address and the applicable deadlines are available should you ever need them. The
          designated address may change, and the current address is always shown on your most recent periodic statement for loan number 1234567890.
          Section 17. Consent to Verify
          You authorize ABC Mortgage Company, and any assignee or servicer of loan number 1234567890, to verify the information you have provided in connection
          with the transaction, including by obtaining consumer reports, verifying employment and income, confirming deposit and asset balances with the institutions
          holding them, obtaining tax return transcripts where you have executed the applicable authorization, and confirming the existence and terms of insurance
          coverage on the property.
          Verification may occur at any time during the origination of the credit and again before closing, and information obtained through verification is used in
          evaluating the credit request and in servicing the account thereafter. Information collected in this manner is handled in accordance with the privacy notice
          furnished to you and with applicable federal and NY law.
          Section 18. Timing Around a Loan Transfer or Payoff
          A servicer’s obligation to respond ends with respect to a submission received more than one year after the loan was discharged or after servicing was
          transferred, and a submission received during that period is answered by the servicer to whom it is properly directed. Address a submission to the party that
          serviced the account during the period in question.
          Where a submission concerns a payoff figure and the loan has since been paid, the seven-business-day deadline applicable to payoff assertions continues to
          govern. Retain your payoff statement, the remittance confirmation, and the paid-in-full acknowledgment, since those three documents resolve nearly every
          question that arises after a loan is satisfied.

Notice Regarding Hazard Insurance Placement
ABC MORTGAGE COMPANY — NOTICE REGARDING HAZARD INSURANCE PLACEMENT
Loan #1234567890 · ABC Mortgage Company · 11/27/2024
Document LN-1959 · Rev. 3.1 · In effect as of 01/15/2024



Nothing in this document changes the interest rate, payment amount, or maturity date of your loan. This informational notice is furnished to John Doe at
the origination of loan number 1234567890 to explain, in advance, the circumstances under which ABC Mortgage Company or a subsequent servicer
may obtain hazard insurance on the property located at 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345 at your expense, and the notices you would receive
before that occurs. No action is required of you at this time, and this notice does not indicate that any coverage problem exists with respect to your
property. It is provided so that you understand the insurance obligations imposed by your security instrument and the consequences of allowing required
coverage to lapse at any point during the life of the loan.

(a) Your Duty to Insure the Property
The security instrument you sign at closing requires you to keep the improvements on the property insured against loss by fire, hazards included within the
term "extended coverage," and any other hazards for which insurance is required, in the amounts and for the periods that the lender requires. The carrier you
select must be acceptable, and the policy must name the lender and its successors and assigns as mortgagee or loss payee so that the lender receives notice
of cancellation and is protected in the event of loss.

You choose your own insurance provider, and nothing in this notice restricts that choice. The coverage must remain continuously in force for the entire term of
the loan, and a policy that is cancelled, not renewed, or reduced below the required amount does not satisfy the obligation even if the lapse is brief or
inadvertent. You should also furnish evidence of coverage to the servicer at each renewal.

(b) Applicable Law and Compliance
This document and the transaction it concerns are subject to the federal statutes and regulations governing residential mortgage credit and to the law of the
State of NY. Where federal law preempts or supplements state law as to a particular matter, federal law controls as to that matter; where state law affords you a
greater protection that is not preempted, that protection applies.

If a change in law or regulation requires a provision of this document to be modified, the provision is deemed amended to the minimum extent necessary to
bring it into compliance, and the remainder continues in effect. No provision should be construed to require any act that applicable law prohibits, or to prohibit
any act that applicable law requires.

(c) About Lender-Placed Coverage
Lender-placed insurance, also called force-placed or creditor-placed insurance, is a policy that a servicer purchases when it has a reasonable basis to believe
that required coverage on a mortgaged property is not in force. The policy protects the lender's interest in the improvements. It is typically written on a blanket
or master program, is more expensive than a policy you would obtain yourself, and its cost is charged to your account.

Lender-placed coverage is materially narrower than a standard homeowners policy. It generally does not insure your personal property, does not provide
liability coverage, does not pay for additional living expenses if the dwelling becomes uninhabitable, and may insure only the outstanding balance of the loan
rather than the full replacement cost of the structure. For those reasons it is never an economical substitute for coverage you obtain directly.

(d) Telephone Communications and Call Monitoring
Telephone calls between you and ABC Mortgage Company may be monitored or recorded for quality assurance, training, and recordkeeping purposes, and
you consent to that monitoring and recording by continuing with a call after being advised of it. Recordings are retained in accordance with our records
schedule and are used only for the purposes described here and as applicable law otherwise permits or requires.

By providing a telephone number in connection with this transaction, you agree that we, our affiliates, our agents, and our service providers may contact you at
that number regarding the account, including by using an automatic dialing system or a prerecorded or artificial voice, and by text message, to the extent
permitted by applicable law. Message and data rates charged by your carrier may apply to any text message you receive.

You may withdraw consent to be contacted at a particular number, or ask that we use a different number or another method entirely, by notifying us at (555)
555-0120 or in writing at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY 12345. Withdrawing consent for automated calls does not prevent us from delivering the notices that
law requires, which may still be sent by mail or by another permitted method.

(e) Advance Notices
A servicer may not charge you for lender-placed insurance unless it has first sent a written notice at least forty-five (45) days before assessing any premium.
That notice states that the servicer lacks evidence of required coverage, identifies the coverage the servicer requires, states that lender-placed insurance may
be more expensive and narrower than a policy you obtain yourself, and requests that you provide evidence of your existing coverage.

A second, reminder notice is sent no earlier than thirty (30) days after the first and at least fifteen (15) days before any charge is assessed. If you provide
evidence of coverage at any point before the placement, no lender-placed policy is purchased. The notices are mailed to your address of record, which is
another reason to keep your contact information current with the servicer.




                                                              Retain this document with your loan file records.                                           Page 1 of 4
(f) Evidence That Satisfies the Requirement
Acceptable evidence normally consists of a copy of the declarations page of your policy, or a certificate or binder issued by your insurance agent, showing the
insured property address, the policy number, the effective and expiration dates, the coverage amounts, and the mortgagee clause naming the lender. Where a
lapse has occurred and coverage has since been reinstated, the evidence should show that coverage was continuous or identify the period of the gap.

Evidence may be submitted by mail to 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY 12345, by facsimile or secure upload where those channels are offered, or through your
insurance agent, who may transmit it directly on your behalf. Referencing loan number 1234567890 on every submission allows the document to be matched
to your account without delay.

(g) Termination of Placed Coverage
If a lender-placed policy has been purchased and you later provide evidence that acceptable coverage was in force, the servicer must cancel the placed policy
within fifteen (15) days of receiving that evidence, refund all premiums and related fees charged for any period of overlapping coverage, and remove the
corresponding charge from your account. A corrected account statement reflecting the adjustment is then issued.

Where coverage genuinely lapsed for a period, the placed policy remains in force for that gap and the premium attributable to it remains payable. Obtaining
your own policy promptly is therefore the most effective way to limit the cost. The servicer will not continue placed coverage beyond the point at which
acceptable evidence of your own insurance takes effect.

(h) Flood Insurance Placement
Separate federal rules apply where the property is located in a special flood hazard area and required flood coverage is not maintained. In that circumstance
the servicer must notify you and, if coverage is not obtained within forty-five (45) days, must purchase flood insurance on your behalf at your expense. The
general notice concerning flood insurance furnished to you separately describes the determination applicable to 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345.

Flood and hazard coverage are distinct requirements, and evidence of one does not satisfy the other. Where both are required, both must be maintained
continuously, and a lapse in either permits placement of the corresponding coverage under the rules applicable to that line.

(i) Property Address and Occupancy of Record
Our records identify the property securing loan number 1234567890 as 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345, and they reflect the occupancy status certified
in your application. Certain program requirements, insurance obligations, and tax treatments depend upon that status, and it is therefore recorded as of the
date of the transaction and carried forward until we are notified of a change.

Notify us if the mailing address at which you wish to receive correspondence differs from the property address, and notify us again if either changes. A mailing
address that differs from the property address is common and is recorded without any effect on the terms of the loan; what matters is that both are accurate so
that notices and bills reach the right place.

Where a change in the use or occupancy of the property is contemplated, review the security instrument and any rider attached to it, since some contain
provisions concerning occupancy, leasing, or transfer of the property. Consult your own adviser concerning the effect of a contemplated change before it is
made.

(j) Keeping Coverage in Force
The most reliable way to avoid lender-placed coverage is to keep your own policy in force, to pay premiums on time, and to confirm at each renewal that the
mortgagee clause names the current servicer at the current address. If servicing is transferred, notify your insurance agent so that renewal declarations are
sent to the correct party; a policy that lists a prior servicer may not generate the evidence the current servicer needs.

Review your coverage periodically to confirm that the dwelling limit remains adequate as construction costs change and that any deductible, particularly a wind,
hail, or named-storm deductible, remains acceptable to you. Adequate coverage protects your own equity in the property, not merely the interest of the lender.

(k) Third-Party Service Providers
We engage third parties to perform functions in connection with the origination and servicing of residential mortgage loans, including document preparation,
data processing, payment processing, tax and flood determination services, insurance tracking, appraisal management, printing, and mailing. Those providers
receive only the information necessary to perform the service for which they are engaged.

Each provider is bound by contract to maintain the confidentiality and security of the information disclosed to it and to use that information only for the purposes
of the engagement. Engaging a service provider does not relieve us of responsibility for the performance of the function delegated, and inquiries concerning
any such function may be directed to us rather than to the provider.

assistance in reading or completing any document relating to loan number 1234567890, contact us at (555) 555-0120 and we will make reasonable
arrangements at no charge to you.

A request for an alternative format has no effect on the evaluation of an application, on the terms available to you, or on the servicing of your account, and no
record of such a request is used for any purpose other than fulfilling it. If you use an assistive technology that has difficulty with a document we have provided,
we welcome that information so that our materials may be improved.

(o) Continuation and Renewal of Placed Coverage
If a lender-placed policy has been purchased and the account still lacks evidence of your own coverage as the placed policy approaches expiration, the
servicer may renew the placed coverage, and it must send renewal notices comparable to those required before the initial placement. Each renewal cycle
carries its own premium charge.

The renewal notices are your opportunity to end the placement by supplying evidence of your own policy. A placed policy does not lapse quietly, and continuing
to carry it is materially more expensive over time than replacing it with coverage you obtain from an agent of your choosing.

(r) Coverage Amounts and Valuation
A placed policy is typically written for an amount tied to the last known coverage on the property, to the replacement cost estimated by the placement carrier, or
to the outstanding principal balance, subject to the requirements of applicable law. That amount protects the lender's interest and may be substantially less
than the amount required to rebuild the dwelling.

If a loss occurred while placed coverage was in effect, proceeds would be applied in accordance with the security instrument and would ordinarily be
insufficient to restore the property fully, and no proceeds would be available for personal property, liability claims, or living expenses. The gap between placed
coverage and a standard homeowners policy is the practical reason to maintain your own.

        Interest Rate Lock-In  Policy and Agreement   Terms
        ABC MORTGAGE COMPANY — INTEREST RATE LOCK-IN POLICY
        Loan #1234567890 : ABC Mortgage Company « 12/02/2024
        Form MTG-2096 : Rev. 4.4 - Effective 12/09/2023
        Where this document summarizes the law, the law itself controls in the event of any difference. This document describes the policy of ABC Mortgage
         Company concerning interest rate lock-in agreements for residential mortgage transactions, including the application identified as loan number
         4234567890 for the property at 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345. A rate lock is a commitment, for a stated period and subject to stated conditions,
         to make credit available to John Doe at a specified interest rate and point combination. The specific rate, points, lock period, and expiration date
         applicable to your transaction, if a lock has been established, appear on the separate rate lock confirmation issued to you; this policy explains the rules
         that govern locks generally.
         1) Choosing to Lock
         Until a lock is established, the rate applicable to your transaction floats, meaning that the rate available to you moves with the market and is not determined
         until a lock is taken or, at the fatest, until the point at which the loan documents are prepared. A floating rate exposes you to the possibility of both improvement
         and deterioration in pricing before closing.
         Locking fixes the rate and points for the lock period, transferring the risk of market movement during that period to the lender, which manages the exposure
         through its own hedging arrangements. Neither choice is inherently better; the decision depends on your tolerance for uncertainty, the time remaining before
         closing, and the state of the market when the decision is made.
         2) How a Lock Is Taken
         A lock is established only when we confirm it in writing. An oral discussion of available pricing, a rate quoted in a marketing communication, a rate shown on an
         initial Loan Estimate issued before a lock, and a rate discussed in general conversation are not locks and create no commitment. If you have not received a
         written lock confirmation identifying the rate, the points, the lock period, and the expiration date, your rate is floating.
         Establishing a lock generally requires a complete application, a property address, and a loan program selection, because pricing depends on program,
         occupancy, property type, loan amount, credit score, and loan-to-value ratio. A change in any of those characteristics after a lock is taken may require the lock
         to be repriced under the terms described below.
         3) Reservation of Rights
          No failure or delay on our part in exercising any right, power, or privilege under the loan documents operates as a waiver of it, and no single or partial exercise
         of any right precludes a further exercise of that right or the exercise of any other. Any waiver must be in writing and signed by an authorized officer of ABC
          Mortgage Company to be effective, and it extends only to the specific matter identified in it.
          Our rights and remedies are cumulative and may be exercised concurrently, successively, or in any order. Nothing in this document creates any right in favor of
          a third party, and no course of dealing between you and us, and no accommodation extended on one occasion, varies the written terms of the loan documents
          or establishes a practice on which either party may rely thereafter.
          Correspondingly, nothing in this document waives, limits, or diminishes any right, protection, or remedy available to you under federal law or under the law of
          NY. To the extent any provision of this document is inconsistent with such a right, the right controls and the remaining provisions continue in effect.
          4) Translation and Language Access
          This document is provided in English. If English is not your primary language, you may wish to have it reviewed with the assistance of a translator or an adviser
          of your choosing before you rely upon it. Where we make a translated version of a document available, the translation is furnished as a courtesy; unless
          applicable law provides otherwise, the English version governs the rights and obligations of the parties.
          Free language assistance is available through the housing counseling organizations identified in the notice furnished to you concerning the availability of
          counseling, many of which offer services in multiple languages. If you require assistance in communicating with us about loan number 1234567890, call (555)
          555-0120 and identify the language you prefer so that we may make appropriate arrangements.
          5) Effect on Your Loan Documents
          This document supplements the note, the security instrument, and the disclosures furnished to you in connection with loan number 1234567890. It does not
          enlarge, reduce, or otherwise modify the amounts payable, the interest rate, the payment schedule, or any right or remedy established by those instruments,
          and no statement here should be read as a representation that any particular term applies to your transaction.
          Where this document summarizes a statute, a regulation, or a program requirement, the summary is provided for convenience. In the event of any difference
          between the summary and the authority summarized, the statute, regulation, or program requirement controls, and no summary in this document limits any
          right afforded to you by law.
           6) Lock Periods and Expiration
           Locks are offered for defined periods, commonly thirty, forty-five, or sixty days, and longer periods are available for certain programs at a price that reflects the
           additional exposure. The lock expires at the close of business on the expiration date shown on the confirmation. A lock must be valid on the date the loan is
           funded, not merely on the date the documents are signed.
                                                 Retain this document with your loan file records.        Page 1 of 5
           Select a lock period that accommodates the realistic timeline of your transaction, including underwriting, appraisal, title work, and any condition likely to require
           time to satisfy. A lock period that is too short frequently resuits in an extension fee that exceeds what the longer period would have cost at the outset.
           7) Expiration and Relock
           If a lock expires and the loan has not closed, pricing reverts to the market. A relock is generally offered at the worse of the original locked pricing and the
           current market pricing, a convention that prevents a lock from operating as an option to be abandoned when the market improves. The terms of any relock are
           confirmed to you in writing before they are applied.
          Where expiration results from a delay attributable to us rather than to you or to a third party, the circumstances are reviewed and an accommodation may be
          extended, Requests for such review should be directed to the office identified at the end of this policy and should describe the sequence of events giving rise to
          the delay.
          8) Changes That Affect a Lock
          A lock is issued on the basis of the transaction characteristics known when it is taken. A change in the loan amount, the loan program or term, the property type
          or occupancy, the credit score used for qualification, the appraised value, or the borrowers obligated on the loan may require the lock to be repriced under the
          applicable pricing adjustments, whether the adjustment operates in your favor or against it.
          A change in the property itself terminates a lock. A lock is specific to the property identified on the confirmation, and applying the pricing to a different property
          requires a new lock at the market available on the date of the change. Notify us promptly of any change so that repricing can be evaluated before it affects your
          closing.
          9) Computation of Time Periods
          Unless a particular statute, regulation, or provision states otherwise, a period expressed in days is measured in calendar days, the day of the act or event that
          Starts the period is excluded, and the last day is included. Where the last day falls on a Saturday, a Sunday, or a legal public holiday, the period runs to the end
          of the next day that is not one of those days.
          Several requirements applicable to residential mortgage transactions are measured in business days, and the definition of a business day differs among them:
          one rule counts days on which our offices are open for substantially all business, while another counts all calendar days except Sundays and legal public
          holidays. Where a specific count controls a right or a deadline, it is stated in the provision that establishes it.
          Where a period is measured from the delivery of a document, delivery by mail is generally presumed to occur three business days after mailing unless earlier
          receipt is documented. Because these conventions determine real deadlines in your transaction, confirm the applicable dates with us or with your settlement
          agent rather than estimating them.
          10) Lock Terms and Your Disclosures
          Taking a lock is a permitted event for issuing a revised Loan Estimate reflecting the locked rate and any point or credit associated with it. The revised estimate
          must be delivered no later than three business days after the lock is established. Points, lender credits, and rate-dependent charges become subject to zero
          tolerance once the rate is locked.
         The interest rate shown on your final Closing Disclosure is the locked rate, and the charges shown reflect the locked Pricing. If you observe a discrepancy
         between your lock confirmation and your disclosures, raise it before closing so that it can be reconciled while a correction remains straightforward.
         11) Compliance With Applicable Law
         This document and the transaction it concerns are subject to the federal statutes and regulations governing residential mortgage credit and to the law of the
         State of NY. Where federal law preempts or supplements state law as to a particular matter, federal law controls as to that matter; where state law affords you a
         greater protection that is not preempted, that protection applies.
         If a change in law or regulation requires a Provision of this document to be modified, the provision is deemed amended to the minimum extent necessary to
         bring it into compliance, and the remainder continues in effect. No provision should be construed to require any act that applicable law prohibits, or to prohibit
         any act that applicable law requires.
         12) Fraud Prevention
         Mortgage transactions attract fraud, most commonly in the form of messages that appear to come from a lender, a settlement agent, or a real estate
         professional and that direct funds to an account controlled by a criminal. We do not transmit wiring instructions by electronic message, and we do not change
         previously issued remittance instructions by electronic message. Verify any such instruction by telephone at a number you have independently confirmed
         before transferring funds.
         Report a suspicious communication concerning loan number 1234567890 to us at (555) 555-0120 promptly, and preserve the message rather than deleting it.
         If funds have already been transmitted, contact your financial institution immediately and ask that a recall be initiated; the prospects of recovery diminish
         sharply within hours, and prompt action is by far the most important factor.

        not guarantee that the transaction will close.

         prediction or a commitment. The decision to lock orto float belongs to you, and its properly made on the basis of your own tolerance for the risk of @ change
         rather than on a forecast.

          ABC MORTGAGE COMPANY — NOTICE REGARDING HUD-APPROVED COUNSELING ORGANIZATIONS
          Loan #1234567890 - ABC Mortgage Company - 11/15/2024
          Doc. LN-2233 - Version 5.7 « Effective Date 11/02/2023
                                                                                         nnn
          You may request an additional copy of this document at any time at no charge. Federal law requires that ABC Mortgage Company provide John Doe
          with information about homeownership counseling organizations in connection with the application identified as loan number 1234567890 and the
          property located at 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345. Counseling is provided by independent, nonprofit organizations approved by the Department
          of Housing and Urban Development, and it is available whether or not you are experiencing any difficulty. This notice explains what counseling agencies
          do, how to locate one serving your area of NY, what a session typically costs, and how to protect yourself against organizations that charge for services
          the approved agencies provide at little or no cost.
          (a) Why You Receive This Notice
          A lender must provide a written list of homeownership counseling organizations, drawn from a source maintained for that purpose, no later than three business
          days after receiving a mortgage application. The list identifies organizations located in or serving the area of the property, together with the services each offers
          and the languages in which those services are available. The list accompanies this notice or is furnished with your initial disclosure package.
          The requirement applies to every applicant. Receiving the list does not suggest that we believe you need counseling, does not affect the evaluation of your
          application, and does not obligate you to contact any organization. Many borrowers find a session useful nonetheless, particularly when purchasing a first
          home or when considering how a payment will fit within a household budget over the long term.
          (b) Headings and Construction
          The headings and numbering used in this document are inserted for convenience of reference only and do not affect the interpretation of any provision. Words
          in the singular include the plural and the reverse, references to any statute or regulation include any successor provision and any rule issued under it, and the
          word "including" means "including without limitation" wherever it appears.
          This document is to be read together with the other loan documents so that all are given effect. Where a genuine conflict exists that cannot be reconciled by
          reading the documents together, the provision that is more specific to the matter in question governs, and as between a provision of this document and a
          mandatory requirement of applicable law, the requirement of law controls.
          (c) What Counseling Agencies Do
          Approved agencies offer pre-purchase counseling covering budgeting, credit, the mortgage process, and the responsibilities of ownership; post-purchase
          counseling addressing maintenance, insurance, and taxes; rental counseling; reverse-mortgage counseling for older homeowners: and default and foreclosure-
          prevention counseling for households facing hardship. Many also administer or can identify down-payment assistance programs available in NY.
         A counselor reviews your circumstances with you, explains the options available, and helps you evaluate them. Counselors do not sell mortgage products,
          receive no compensation contingent on your choice of lender or loan, and have no financial interest in whether your transaction closes. That independence is
         the principal value of the service.
         (d) Locating a Counseling Agency
         The written list furnished with this notice identifies organizations serving your area. You may also obtain a current list from the Department of Housing and
         Urban Development's counseling agency locator, which may be searched by state, county, ZIP code, and service type, or by calling the department's toll-free
         housing counseling line, which operates around the clock and offers assistance in multiple languages.
         Agencies vary in the services they emphasize and in their capacity at any given time. If the first organization you contact cannot schedule a session promptly,
         ask whether it can refer you to another approved agency serving the same area, or select an alternative from the list rather than turning to an unapproved
         provider.
         (e) Requests for Copies of Documents
         You may request a copy of any document relating to loan number 1234567890 that we hold, including the note, the security instrument, the closing disclosures,
         a payment history, or an escrow analysis. Requests should be made in writing at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY 12345 or through the secure channel identified
         on your statement, and should identify the documents sought and the period they cover.
         Copies of recent documents are ordinarily provided without charge. A reasonable fee may be assessed, to the extent permitted by applicable law, for a request
         requiring historical research, for the reproduction of a voluminous record, or for expedited delivery; any such fee is disclosed to you before it is incurred, and
         you may withdraw or narrow the request instead.
         Certain requests are governed by the Servicing rules described in the notice concerning error resolution and information requests, which impose specific
         acknowledgment and response deadlines when the request is sent to the designated address. Using that address for a documentary request is generally to
         your advantage.
         (f) Cost of Counseling
         Many approved organizations provide counseling free of charge, supported by grants and other funding. Some charge a modest fee for particular services,
         such as a comprehensive pre-purchase session or a homebuyer education certificate required by a down-payment assistance program. Any fee must be
         disclosed to you in advance, and an approved agency may not deny service on the basis of inability to pay where the service is grant-funded.
                                               Retain this document with your loan file records.        Page | of 4
           Foreclosure-prevention and default counseling are provided without charge by approved agencies. No borrower should ever Pay an upfront fee to obtain
           assistance with a mortgage payment problem, and a demand for such a fee is the clearest indicator that the organization making it is not an approved
           counseling agency.
           (g) Computation of Time Periods
           Unless a particular statute, regulation, or provision states otherwise, a period expressed in days is measured in calendar days, the day of the act or event that
           Starts the period is excluded, and the last day is included. Where the last day falls on a Saturday, a Sunday, or a legal public holiday, the period runs to the end
          of the next day that is not one of those days.
          Several requirements applicable to residential mortgage transactions are measured in business days, and the definition of a business day differs among them:
          one rule counts days on which our offices are open for substantially all business, while another counts all calendar days except Sundays and legal public
          holidays. Where a specific count controls a right or a deadline, it is stated in the provision that establishes it.
          Where a period is measured from the delivery of a document, delivery by mail is generally presumed to occur three business days after mailing unless earlier
          receipt is documented. Because these conventions determine real deadlines in your transaction, confirm the applicable dates with us or with your settlement
          agent rather than estimating them.
          (h) Recordkeeping and Document Retention
          We retain the records relating to this transaction, including the loan documents, disclosures, notices, and correspondence, for the periods required by
          applicable law and by our own records-management schedule, and for such longer period as any examination, inquiry, or proceeding may require. Records are
          maintained in a form that permits accurate reproduction, whether the original was created on paper or electronically, and a reproduction is treated as an original
          for all ordinary purposes.
          You are encouraged to keep your own permanent file containing the note, the security instrument, the closing disclosures, each annual escrow analysis and
          interest statement, and evidence of your insurance and tax payments. Documents of that kind are frequently needed years later in connection with a refinance,
          a tax question, an insurance claim, or the sale of the property at 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345, and reconstructing them after the fact can be slow and
          may involve a research fee.
         (i) Preparing for a Session
         A session is most productive if you bring recent pay statements, your most recent tax returns and W-2 forms, statements for checking, savings, and retirement
         accounts, a list of monthly obligations, and a copy of any correspondence relevant to the matter you wish to discuss. For a session concerning an existing loan,
         bring the most recent periodic Statement and any notice you have received.
         Sessions are offered in person, by telephone, and, increasingly, by video conference. Counseling records are confidential and are not shared with a lender
         without your written consent; a counselor working with you on your transaction may, at your request, communicate with us on your behalf, and we cooperate
         with such requests.
         (i) Consent to Verify
         You authorize ABC Mortgage Company, and any assignee or servicer of loan number 1234567890, to verify the information you have provided in connection
         with the transaction, including by obtaining consumer reports, verifying employment and income, confirming deposit and asset balances with the institutions
         holding them, obtaining tax return transcripts where you have executed the applicable authorization, and confirming the existence and terms of insurance
         coverage on the property.
         Verification may occur at any time during the origination of the credit and again before closing, and information obtained through verification is used in
         evaluating the credit request and in servicing the account thereafter. Information collected in this manner is handled in accordance with the privacy notice
         furnished to you and with applicable federal and NY law.
        (k) Assistance Directly From the Servicer
        Counseling supplements, and does not replace, direct communication with the servicer of your loan. If a change in circumstances ever affects your ability to
        make a payment on loan number 1234567890, contacting the servicer early generally produces the widest range of options. Assistance programs typically
        require documentation and take time to evaluate, and early contact preserves that time.
        A counselor may participate in those discussions with you and can help you assemble the documentation an assistance review requires. Working with an
        approved agency does not limit any option otherwise available to you and does not affect how your account is serviced.
        (!) Protecting Yourself Against Fraud
        Mortgage transactions attract fraud, most commonly in the form of messages that appear to come from a lender, a settlement agent, or a real estate
        professional and that direct funds to an account controlled by a criminal. We do not transmit wiring instructions by electronic message, and we do not change
        previously issued remittance instructions by electronic message. Verify any such instruction by telephone at a number you have independently confirmed
        before transferring funds.
        Report a suspicious communication concerning loan number 1234567890 to us at (555) 555-0120 promptly, and preserve the message rather than deleting it.
        If funds have already been transmitted, contact your financial institution immediately and ask that a recall be initiated; the prospects of recovery diminish
        sharply within hours, and Prompt action is by far the most important factor.

         (r) Post-Purchase and Financial Counseling

        proposed consolidation, a home equity product, or a refinance offer that arrives in the mail is actually to your advantage — an assessment that is difficult to
        make from marketing material alone.
        (s) What Counseling Does Not Do

        compel any lender or servicer to grant a request. Its role is advisory, and its value lies in the independence and experience of the counselor rather than in any
        authority over the transaction.

        agreement executed by the parties, and you should treat a counselor's general description of what is typically available as guidance rather than as a

Loan #1234567890 · ABC Mortgage Company · 11/30/2024

A copy of this document is retained in the file maintained for loan number 1234567890. This Privacy Notice describes how ABC Mortgage Company
("ABC Mortgage Company," "we," "us," or "our") collects, shares, and protects the personal information of consumers and customers in connection with
the loan identified as 1234567890 and the related residential financing secured by the property located at 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345.
Financial companies choose how they share your personal information, and federal law gives consumers the right to limit some but not all sharing. This
notice also explains the choices available to you and how you may exercise them. Please read it carefully and retain a copy with your loan records. The
provisions of this notice apply throughout the life of your account and after the relationship ends, except as otherwise required or permitted by law.

Purpose of This Notice
Financial companies choose how they share your personal information, and federal law, including the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act and its implementing
regulations, requires us to tell you how we collect, share, and protect that information. We are providing this notice so that you understand what we do and the
choices you may have. The types of personal information we collect and share depend on the product or service you have with us and on the nature of our
relationship. We furnish this notice when you become a customer and, as required by applicable law, on a periodic basis for so long as you maintain a
continuing relationship with ABC Mortgage Company.

When you are no longer our customer, we continue to share your information as described in this notice, subject to the limitations imposed by law. Nothing in
this notice is intended to expand or restrict any rights you may have under other agreements between you and ABC Mortgage Company or under applicable
federal and state law. If state law provides you with additional rights or protections, we will honor those rights to the extent they apply to your account and to the
information we maintain about you.

What Information We Collect
We collect personal information about you in connection with providing you a financial product or service. The information we collect depends on the product or
service you request and may include your name, address, and telephone number; your Social Security number and date of birth; your income, employment
information, and assets; and your account balances, payment history, and transaction or loss history. We obtain much of this information directly from you on
applications and other forms, and through your communications with us by telephone, in writing, or electronically.

We also collect your personal information from others, such as credit bureaus, affiliates, and other companies. For example, we may receive your credit history,
creditworthiness, and credit scores from consumer reporting agencies, and we may receive verification of employment, deposits, and other account information
from third parties you authorize. We maintain records relating to the origination, servicing, and, where applicable, the transfer of your loan, including documents
you sign at closing and information generated during the life of your account.

The categories of information we collect and the manner in which we use that information may change over time as products, services, and legal requirements
evolve. Where required, we will update this notice to reflect material changes in our information practices. We collect only the personal information reasonably
necessary to provide the products and services you request, to administer your account, and to comply with our legal and regulatory obligations.

How We Share Your Information
All financial companies need to share customers' personal information to run their everyday business. In the section that follows, we describe the reasons
financial companies can share their customers' personal information, the reasons ABC Mortgage Company chooses to share, and whether you can limit that
sharing. Whether you can limit sharing depends on the reason for which the information is shared and on the protections afforded to you by federal and state
law.

We may share your personal information for our everyday business purposes, such as to process your transactions, maintain your account, respond to court
orders and legal investigations, or report to credit bureaus. We may also share for our own marketing purposes, to offer our products and services to you, and
for joint marketing with other financial companies with which we have formal agreements. For these reasons, sharing may occur without your ability to limit it,
except where federal or state law provides otherwise.

We may further share your personal information for purposes related to our affiliates' everyday business, including information about your transactions and
experiences and, in certain circumstances, information about your creditworthiness. Sharing for nonaffiliates to market to you, and certain sharing of credit
information among affiliates, are categories of sharing that you may have the right to limit, as more fully described in the sections of this notice addressing
affiliates, nonaffiliates, and your choices.

Reasons You Cannot Limit Sharing
There are certain everyday business purposes for which federal law does not permit you to limit our sharing of your personal information. These include
sharing necessary to process your transactions, to maintain and service your account, to respond to court orders, subpoenas, and legal investigations, and to
report to credit bureaus and other consumer reporting agencies. We also share as necessary to protect against or prevent actual or potential fraud,
unauthorized transactions, claims, or other liability, and to comply with federal, state, and local laws and regulatory requirements.

In addition, we may disclose your personal information to companies that perform services on our behalf, including providers of document preparation, data
processing, account servicing, mailing, collection, and similar functions. Where we engage such service providers, we require by contract that they maintain the
confidentiality and security of your information and use it only for the limited purposes for which it was disclosed. These disclosures are part of running our
everyday business and are not subject to your right to limit sharing under applicable law.

property. Such disclosures are made consistent with applicable law and the confidentiality safeguards described in this notice.

Escrow Account Establishment and Annual Analysis Disclosure
ABC MORTGAGE COMPANY — ESCROW ACCOUNT DISCLOSURE STATEMENT
Loan #1234567890 · ABC Mortgage Company · 12/05/2024
Doc. LN-2781 · Version 4.9 · Effective Date 06/07/2023



Please read this document in its entirety and retain it with the other papers relating to your loan. This disclosure explains how an escrow account is
established, funded, analyzed, and adjusted in connection with loan number 1234567890 and the property located at 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY
12345. An escrow account is a fund held by the servicer from which property taxes, hazard insurance premiums, and similar recurring charges are paid
on your behalf as they come due. The estimates used to establish your account appear on the initial escrow account statement furnished separately;
this document describes the rules that govern the account for the life of the loan, including the cushion permitted by law, the annual analysis, and the
treatment of surpluses and shortages.

1.0 Purpose of the Escrow Account
An escrow account allows the annual cost of property taxes and insurance to be collected in monthly installments together with your principal and interest
payment, rather than in large periodic sums. The servicer holds those funds and disburses them to the taxing authority and to the insurance carrier on or before
the date each obligation becomes due, provided the account contains sufficient funds and the servicer has received the bill or the information necessary to pay
it.

Maintaining an escrow account protects both you and the holder of the security instrument. Unpaid property taxes can become a lien with priority over the
mortgage, and a lapse in hazard coverage leaves the property unprotected against loss. Because those risks are shared, escrow is required for many loan
programs and is offered as an option on most others.

2.0 Items Paid From Escrow
The items escrowed for your account are listed on the initial escrow account statement and typically include general real estate taxes, special assessments
levied by a taxing district, hazard or homeowners insurance premiums, and, where applicable, flood insurance premiums and mortgage insurance premiums.
Items that vary by jurisdiction, such as ground rent or a municipal service charge, may also be escrowed where the loan program requires it.

Charges that are not escrowed remain your direct responsibility. These commonly include homeowners association dues, utility charges, supplemental or
omitted tax assessments issued outside the ordinary billing cycle, and any insurance coverage you elect beyond what the security instrument requires. A
charge is not escrowed merely because a bill for it is received by the servicer, and the servicer will forward or return items it does not administer.

3.0 Initial Funding and the Cushion
At closing, an initial deposit is collected so that the account will hold enough to pay each escrowed item when it first comes due. Federal law permits the
servicer to maintain a cushion of no more than one-sixth of the estimated total annual disbursements, which is equivalent to approximately two monthly escrow
payments. Some loan programs and some state laws permit a smaller cushion, and where they do, the smaller figure controls.

The amount of the initial deposit depends on the month of closing relative to the tax and insurance due dates in NY, and it is calculated so that the projected
low point in the account balance over the coming twelve months equals the permitted cushion. The specific figures for this transaction appear on your Closing
Disclosure and initial escrow account statement and are not restated in this document.

4.0 The Yearly Analysis
At least once each year the servicer conducts an escrow account analysis, comparing the payments actually made from the account with those that were
projected and estimating the disbursements expected during the coming computation year. The analysis produces a new monthly escrow payment and an
annual escrow account statement showing the account history, the projected activity, and the resulting change to your total monthly payment, if any.

The annual statement is furnished to you at least thirty (30) days before the new payment amount takes effect. Escrow payments change most often because a
taxing authority has revised the assessed value or the rate applicable to the property, or because the insurance carrier has adjusted the premium at renewal.
Those amounts are set by third parties, and the servicer neither controls them nor profits from an increase.

5.0 Surpluses and Shortages
A surplus exists when the analysis shows that the account holds more than the target balance plus the permitted cushion. Where the account is current and the
surplus is fifty dollars or more, it is refunded to you within thirty (30) days of the analysis; a smaller surplus may be refunded or credited against future
payments. A shortage exists when the balance is below the target but the account is not overdrawn; you may pay a shortage in a lump sum or allow it to be
collected over the following twelve months.

A deficiency exists when the account balance is negative. Depending on the size of the deficiency and the status of the account, the servicer may require
repayment in a single sum or spread the amount over two to twelve months as permitted by law. In each case, the annual escrow account statement identifies
the condition of the account, states the amount involved, and explains the option being applied for loan number 1234567890.

6.0 What You Must Do
You remain responsible for maintaining the insurance coverage required by the security instrument and for ensuring that the servicer is named as mortgagee or
loss payee on each policy covering 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345. Notify the servicer promptly of any change in carrier, policy number, coverage
amount, or mailing address, and forward any tax or insurance bill that appears to require attention, particularly a supplemental assessment issued outside the
normal cycle.

If you receive a notice of delinquent taxes, a cancellation or non-renewal notice from an insurer, or a bill you believe should have been paid from escrow,
contact the servicer immediately at (555) 555-0120. Prompt notice generally allows an item to be paid before a penalty accrues, and any penalty caused by the
servicer's failure to make a timely disbursement from a properly funded account is borne by the servicer.

7.0 Electronic Delivery
Where you have consented to receive records electronically, this document may be delivered to the electronic address on file or posted to a secure site with
notification to you, and such delivery satisfies any requirement that it be provided in writing. You may withdraw that consent at any time, and you may request a
paper copy of this or any other document delivered electronically, in each case in the manner described in the electronic records consent furnished to you.

If you are unable to access, view, or retain a document delivered electronically, notify us at (555) 555-0120 so that a paper copy may be sent to your address of
record. A request for a paper copy of a particular document is not, by itself, treated as a withdrawal of your consent to electronic delivery of other
communications.

8.0 Timely Disbursement Obligation
The servicer must make escrow disbursements on or before the deadline for payment, or, where a jurisdiction offers a discount for early payment, on or before
the discount date, provided the account contains sufficient funds and the servicer has received the bill or other necessary information. Where the account is
short, the servicer may advance funds to prevent a lapse or a delinquency and may then collect the advance in accordance with applicable law.

Records of every escrow receipt and disbursement are maintained for the life of the loan and are summarized on the annual statement. You may request an
account history at any time. If servicing is transferred, escrow funds transfer with the loan, and the transferee servicer assumes the obligation to make timely
disbursements without interruption.

9.0 Telephone Communications and Call Monitoring
Telephone calls between you and ABC Mortgage Company may be monitored or recorded for quality assurance, training, and recordkeeping purposes, and
you consent to that monitoring and recording by continuing with a call after being advised of it. Recordings are retained in accordance with our records
schedule and are used only for the purposes described here and as applicable law otherwise permits or requires.

By providing a telephone number in connection with this transaction, you agree that we, our affiliates, our agents, and our service providers may contact you at
that number regarding the account, including by using an automatic dialing system or a prerecorded or artificial voice, and by text message, to the extent

You may withdraw consent to be contacted at a particular number, or ask that we use a different number or another method entirely, by notifying us at (555)
555-0120 or in writing at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY 12345. Withdrawing consent for automated calls does not prevent us from delivering the notices that
law requires, which may still be sent by mail or by another permitted method.

10.0 Requests for Copies of Documents
You may request a copy of any document relating to loan number 1234567890 that we hold, including the note, the security instrument, the closing disclosures,
a payment history, or an escrow analysis. Requests should be made in writing at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY 12345 or through the secure channel identified
on your statement, and should identify the documents sought and the period they cover.

Copies of recent documents are ordinarily provided without charge. A reasonable fee may be assessed, to the extent permitted by applicable law, for a request
requiring historical research, for the reproduction of a voluminous record, or for expedited delivery; any such fee is disclosed to you before it is incurred, and
you may withdraw or narrow the request instead.

Certain requests are governed by the servicing rules described in the notice concerning error resolution and information requests, which impose specific
acknowledgment and response deadlines when the request is sent to the designated address. Using that address for a documentary request is generally to
your advantage.

11.0 Interest on Escrow Balances
Federal law does not require that interest be paid on escrow balances. Some states, including certain jurisdictions with escrow-interest statutes, require the
payment of interest at a prescribed rate on funds held for property located within the state. Where NY law imposes such a requirement, interest is credited to
your account in the manner and at the frequency the statute directs, and the credit appears on your annual escrow account statement.

Where no statutory requirement applies, escrow balances do not earn interest for your benefit. Escrow funds are held in a manner consistent with applicable
law and are not commingled with the general funds of the servicer in a way that would defeat their character as funds held for your account.

12.0 Discontinuing an Escrow Account
Where the loan program and the terms of the security instrument permit, you may request that the escrow account be discontinued after the loan has seasoned
and the account is current. Eligibility generally depends upon the loan-to-value ratio, the payment history, the absence of any prior escrow deficiency, and any
applicable investor requirement. A request should be made in writing and referenced to loan number 1234567890.

If an escrow account is closed, any remaining balance is refunded to you within the period required by law and you assume direct responsibility for paying
taxes and insurance premiums as they come due. Failure to pay those items thereafter permits the servicer to reestablish an escrow account, to advance funds
to protect its interest, and to place insurance on the property at your expense as described in the separate notice concerning lender-placed coverage.

13.0 Initial and Annual Statements
The initial escrow account statement is provided at settlement or within forty-five (45) days after the account is established. It itemizes the estimated taxes,
insurance premiums, and other charges expected to be paid from the account during the first twelve months, the anticipated disbursement dates, and the
amount of the cushion.

Thereafter an annual escrow account statement is provided within thirty (30) days after the end of each computation year. It shows the actual activity of the
past year against the projections, the projected activity for the coming year, the new monthly payment, and the reason for any change. Compare each annual
statement to the prior one so that a change in taxes or premiums is understood when it occurs rather than later.

15.0 Escrow at Payoff or Transfer
When the loan is paid in full, any balance remaining in escrow after the final disbursements is refunded to you within the period required by law, and thereafter
you pay taxes and insurance directly. Confirm with the taxing authority and the insurer that future bills are directed to you rather than to the former servicer,
since a bill sent to the wrong party is a common source of a missed payment after a payoff.

When servicing transfers, escrow funds transfer with the loan and the transferee servicer must honor the terms of the existing account, including any payment
arrangement for a shortage. The transferee conducts its own analysis in the ordinary course, and a change in the payment following a transfer reflects that
analysis rather than the transfer itself.

This Equal Credit Opportunity Act Notice is furnished to John Doe by ABC Mortgage Company in connection with loan number 1234567890 and the
credit transaction concerning the property located at 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345. The federal Equal Credit Opportunity Act and its
implementing regulation, Regulation B, prohibit creditors from discriminating against credit applicants on certain prohibited bases and confer upon you
important rights with respect to the evaluation of your application, the disposition of your request for credit, and your access to the reasons underlying
any action taken. ABC Mortgage Company is committed to extending credit to all creditworthy applicants in a fair, consistent, and lawful manner, and
this disclosure summarizes the protections, obligations, and remedies that govern the credit transaction described above as of November 14, 2024. This
document does not require a response from you unless it expressly states otherwise.

1) Prohibited Bases of Discrimination
The Equal Credit Opportunity Act and Regulation B make it unlawful for any creditor, including ABC Mortgage Company, to discriminate against an applicant
with respect to any aspect of a credit transaction on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, or age, provided the applicant has the
capacity to enter into a binding contract. These prohibited bases extend to every phase of the credit relationship, including the taking and evaluation of
applications, the establishment of terms and conditions, the administration of accounts, and the collection of amounts owed. ABC Mortgage Company does not
consider any prohibited basis as a negative factor in its assessment of the creditworthiness of John Doe.

It is further unlawful for a creditor to discriminate against an applicant because all or part of the applicant's income derives from any public assistance program,
or because the applicant has in good faith exercised any right under the Consumer Credit Protection Act. The federal agencies that enforce compliance with
this law may, in appropriate circumstances, consider a creditor's conduct toward applicants who exercise such rights. Accordingly, ABC Mortgage Company
evaluates income from public assistance and other lawful sources on the same terms applied to comparable income, and it does not penalize John Doe for
asserting any statutory right.

These protections apply uniformly regardless of the type, size, or purpose of the credit requested, whether the extension of credit is secured or unsecured, and
whether the transaction is consummated, withdrawn, or denied. ABC Mortgage Company maintains internal policies, training, and monitoring designed to
ensure that personnel involved in the origination, underwriting, and servicing of credit adhere to these requirements at every stage of the transaction
associated with loan number 1234567890.

2) Successors and Assigns
We may sell, assign, transfer, pledge, or otherwise convey the loan, the loan documents, or the right to service the loan, in whole or in part, at any time and
without your consent, except as applicable law requires. A transfer of ownership or of servicing does not by itself change the interest rate, the payment amount,
the maturity date, or any other term of your obligation, and the transferee succeeds to the rights and, to the extent of the transfer, the obligations described in
the loan documents.

This document binds and benefits you and us and our respective heirs, executors, administrators, successors, and permitted assigns. You may not assign or
delegate your rights or obligations without our prior written consent, and the sale or transfer of the property at 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345 does not
release you from liability for the debt unless we expressly agree in writing to a release.

3) Right to a Statement of Reasons
When ABC Mortgage Company takes adverse action on an application for credit, or on an existing account, you have the right under the Equal Credit
Opportunity Act to a statement of the specific reasons for that action. Adverse action includes a denial or revocation of credit, a change in the terms of an
existing account that is not favorable to John Doe and that is not applied to all or substantially all of a class of the creditor's accounts, and a refusal to grant
credit in substantially the amount or on substantially the terms requested in an application.

The statement of specific reasons will either be provided automatically with the notice of adverse action or be made available upon your timely request. If the
reasons are not disclosed in the initial notice, ABC Mortgage Company will include a statement of your right to request the reasons within sixty (60) days of the
notification, together with the name, address, and telephone number of the person or office from which the reasons may be obtained. Upon a timely oral or
written request, ABC Mortgage Company will furnish the specific reasons in writing within a reasonable period of time, generally not exceeding thirty (30) days.

The reasons disclosed will be specific and will indicate the principal factors that influenced the action taken; statements that the action was based on internal
standards or policies, or that the applicant failed to achieve a qualifying score, are not by themselves sufficient. Any statement of reasons furnished in
connection with loan number 1234567890 will accurately reflect the actual basis upon which the credit decision was made.
