Loan Payoff and Lien Release Procedures
ABC MORTGAGE COMPANY — LOAN PAYOFF AND LIEN RELEASE PROCEDURES
Loan #1234567890 · ABC Mortgage Company · 11/23/2024
Document LN-3055 · Rev. 1.5 · In effect as of 03/25/2023



You may request an additional copy of this document at any time at no charge. This document describes how to request a payoff statement for loan
number 1234567890, what such a statement contains, how long it remains valid, and how funds must be remitted in order to satisfy the debt secured by
the property at 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345. A payoff statement is the servicer's official calculation of the total amount required to pay the loan
in full as of a stated date. It is used in connection with a sale, a refinance, or a voluntary prepayment, and it is relied upon by settlement agents and title
insurers. These procedures apply throughout the life of the loan and are provided at origination for your future reference.

Article I. Authorized Requesters
A payoff statement may be requested by you, by a co-borrower obligated on the note, or by a third party you have authorized in writing, such as a settlement
agent, title company, closing attorney, or refinancing lender. A third-party request must be accompanied by a signed borrower authorization identifying the
requesting party and the loan, or the request will be returned without a statement.

Because a payoff statement discloses the outstanding balance and other account information, it is treated as confidential. We do not furnish payoff figures by
telephone to unverified callers, and we do not send statements to an address or electronic destination that is not associated with the account or identified in a
valid authorization. These limitations protect you against payoff fraud, which typically begins with the interception or alteration of a legitimate statement.

Article II. Response Time
An accurate payoff statement is provided within a reasonable time and, in any event, within the period prescribed by applicable federal and NY law, which is
generally not more than seven (7) business days after receipt of a written request, excluding legal public holidays, Saturdays, and Sundays. Where a delay is
caused by a natural disaster, a bankruptcy proceeding, or similar circumstances, the period may be extended to the extent the law allows.

Requests submitted through an established settlement-agent channel are frequently fulfilled more quickly. To avoid pressure at the end of a transaction, we
recommend ordering the statement as soon as a closing date is set rather than in the final days before funding.

Article III. Relationship to Your Other Loan Documents
This document supplements the note, the security instrument, and the disclosures furnished to you in connection with loan number 1234567890. It does not
enlarge, reduce, or otherwise modify the amounts payable, the interest rate, the payment schedule, or any right or remedy established by those instruments,
and no statement here should be read as a representation that any particular term applies to your transaction.

Where this document summarizes a statute, a regulation, or a program requirement, the summary is provided for convenience. In the event of any difference
between the summary and the authority summarized, the statute, regulation, or program requirement controls, and no summary in this document limits any
right afforded to you by law.

Article IV. Accessibility and Alternative Formats
We endeavor to make our communications accessible. If you require this or any other document in an alternative format, including large print, or if you need
assistance in reading or completing any document relating to loan number 1234567890, contact us at (555) 555-0120 and we will make reasonable
arrangements at no charge to you.

A request for an alternative format has no effect on the evaluation of an application, on the terms available to you, or on the servicing of your account, and no
record of such a request is used for any purpose other than fulfilling it. If you use an assistive technology that has difficulty with a document we have provided,
we welcome that information so that our materials may be improved.

Article V. Third-Party Service Providers
We engage third parties to perform functions in connection with the origination and servicing of residential mortgage loans, including document preparation,
data processing, payment processing, tax and flood determination services, insurance tracking, appraisal management, printing, and mailing. Those providers
receive only the information necessary to perform the service for which they are engaged.

Each provider is bound by contract to maintain the confidentiality and security of the information disclosed to it and to use that information only for the purposes
of the engagement. Engaging a service provider does not relieve us of responsibility for the performance of the function delegated, and inquiries concerning
any such function may be directed to us rather than to the provider.

Article VI. This Document Is Not Advice
This document is furnished for informational purposes and summarizes requirements, policies, or procedures in general terms. It does not constitute legal, tax,
accounting, insurance, or investment advice, and neither ABC Mortgage Company nor any of its employees or agents is acting as your adviser in any of those
capacities. Statements made here are necessarily general and may not address the particular facts of your situation.

Article VII. Contents of the Statement
A payoff statement identifies the unpaid principal balance, interest accrued through the payoff date, the per diem interest rate applicable after that date, any
escrow advance or shortage, recording or reconveyance charges, statement or wire fees where permitted, and any other amount properly due under the loan
documents. It states the date through which the quoted figure is good and the exact remittance instructions.

The statement does not reflect payments that have not yet been received or that have not cleared, and it does not anticipate a payment returned for insufficient
funds after the statement date. If a scheduled monthly payment is made after the statement is issued, the payoff amount changes, and the settlement agent
should confirm the figure before disbursing.

Article VIII. Per Diem Interest and Expiration
Interest accrues daily on the unpaid principal balance. If funds are received after the good-through date shown on the statement, additional per diem interest is
due for each day beyond that date, and a short payoff leaves a residual balance that keeps the lien in place. Settlement agents ordinarily include several days
of additional per diem to avoid this outcome.

A statement that has expired should not be relied upon. Request an updated statement whenever the closing is postponed past the good-through date,
whenever a monthly payment is made after the statement is issued, or whenever a charge such as a property inspection or escrow disbursement occurs in the
interim.

Article IX. Remittance Instructions and Wire Fraud
Payoff funds must be remitted exactly as the statement directs, whether by wire transfer, certified funds, or cashier's check. Wiring instructions appear only on
the statement itself. We do not change remittance instructions by email, and any message purporting to convey revised wiring instructions should be treated as
fraudulent until verified by telephone with our office at a number you have independently confirmed.

Funds sent to an incorrect destination are not credited to your account and do not satisfy the debt. Because payoff wire fraud is a persistent risk in residential
transactions, we ask that you and your settlement agent verify instructions verbally before initiating any transfer of funds relating to loan number 1234567890.

Article X. Lien Release After Payoff
After the loan is paid in full and the funds have cleared, we execute and record a release, satisfaction, or reconveyance of the security instrument within the
period required by NY law, and we forward the cancelled note or a paid-in-full acknowledgment to you. Recording timelines depend upon the practices of the
county recorder and may take several weeks after the release is submitted.

Retain your paid-in-full letter and the recorded release permanently. Those documents establish that the lien on 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345 has
been discharged, and they are the fastest way to resolve a title question arising years later. If you have not received evidence of release within sixty (60) days
of payoff, contact us so that the recording may be traced.

materially affects your rights or obligations, we will furnish a revised document or a notice describing the change in the manner and within the time that

These procedures are provided as of November 14, 2024 and may be updated from time to time to reflect changes in law or in our operations. Current

Article XIII. Fraud Prevention
Mortgage transactions attract fraud, most commonly in the form of messages that appear to come from a lender, a settlement agent, or a real estate
professional and that direct funds to an account controlled by a criminal. We do not transmit wiring instructions by electronic message, and we do not change
previously issued remittance instructions by electronic message. Verify any such instruction by telephone at a number you have independently confirmed
before transferring funds.

Report a suspicious communication concerning loan number 1234567890 to us at (555) 555-0120 promptly, and preserve the message rather than deleting it.
If funds have already been transmitted, contact your financial institution immediately and ask that a recall be initiated; the prospects of recovery diminish
sharply within hours, and prompt action is by far the most important factor.

applicable law and by our own records-management schedule, and for such longer period as any examination, inquiry, or proceeding may require. Records are

maintained in a form that permits accurate reproduction, whether the original was created on paper or electronically, and a reproduction is treated as an original
for all ordinary purposes.

interest statement, and evidence of your insurance and tax payments. Documents of that kind are frequently needed years later in connection with a refinance,

Article XV. Payoff in Connection With a Refinance
In a refinance, the new lender or its settlement agent orders the payoff statement, and the existing loan is satisfied from the proceeds of the new loan. Because
a refinance secured by your principal residence may carry a right of rescission, funding may occur several days after signing, and the payoff statement must
remain valid through the actual disbursement date rather than the signing date.

Do not stop making payments on the existing loan while a refinance is pending. Until the payoff funds are received and applied, the existing obligation
continues in full force, and a payment skipped in anticipation of a closing that is delayed produces a delinquency that may be reported and that may itself
jeopardize the new transaction.

Article XVI. Effect of an Unenforceable Provision
If any provision of this document is held by a court or other tribunal of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, that holding shall not affect
any other provision, and the remainder shall continue in full force and effect as though the offending provision had never been included. The parties intend that
each provision be severable and that this document be given effect to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law.

Where a provision is unenforceable only because it exceeds a limit imposed by law, it shall be deemed reduced or reformed to the maximum extent the law
permits and enforced as so modified, so as to give effect to the original intent to the greatest degree possible. Nothing in this document waives or limits any
right afforded to you by a mandatory provision of federal law or of the law of NY.

Article XVII. After the Loan Is Paid
Following payoff you receive a paid-in-full acknowledgment, a refund of any escrow balance and overpayment, and, in due course, evidence that the lien has
been released of record. Any automatic payment arrangement you maintain should be canceled by you with your own financial institution, since a recurring
debit you established is not within the servicer's control.

Notify your insurance carrier and the taxing authority that the loan has been satisfied so that future bills and refunds are directed to you. Where an escrow
account existed, the next tax or insurance bill after payoff is your direct responsibility, and the transition is the point at which such an obligation is most often
overlooked.

Notice of Property Located in a Special Flood Hazard Area
ABC MORTGAGE COMPANY — NOTICE OF PROPERTY LOCATED IN A SPECIAL FLOOD HAZARD AREA
Loan #1234567890 · ABC Mortgage Company · 12/03/2024
Doc. LN-3329 · Version 3.1 · Effective Date 01/10/2023



This document supersedes any earlier version of the same document furnished to you. Federal law requires ABC Mortgage Company to determine
whether the property offered as security for loan number 1234567890, located at 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345, is situated in an area identified
by the Federal Emergency Management Agency as having special flood hazards, and to notify John Doe of that determination. The Standard Flood
Hazard Determination Form completed for this transaction states the result and accompanies this notice or is delivered with your disclosure package.
This document explains what the determination means, when flood insurance is required, how coverage amounts are calculated, and what occurs if
required coverage is not maintained.

1. The Determination
A flood hazard determination identifies the flood zone in which the improvements lie, by reference to the Flood Insurance Rate Map covering the community,
and states whether the community participates in the National Flood Insurance Program. The determination is made by a third-party provider engaged for that
purpose and is documented on the Standard Flood Hazard Determination Form retained in the loan file.

Zones beginning with the letter A or V are special flood hazard areas, in which the requirement to maintain flood insurance applies. Zones designated X, B, or
C are outside the special flood hazard area, and coverage is not federally required, although the risk of flooding is never zero and coverage remains available
and frequently inexpensive in those zones.

2. Credit Reporting
We may furnish information about the status and payment history of loan number 1234567890 to one or more consumer reporting agencies, and we do so in
accordance with the accuracy and dispute-handling requirements that federal law imposes on furnishers. Information furnished ordinarily includes the account
type, the date opened, the balance, the scheduled payment, and the payment status as of the reporting date.

If you believe that information we have furnished about this account is inaccurate or incomplete, you may notify us in writing at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY
12345, describing the item and the reason you believe it to be incorrect and enclosing any supporting documentation. We will investigate, report the results to
you, and correct any inaccuracy with each agency to which the information was furnished.

You may also dispute the item directly with the consumer reporting agency, which must generally conduct its own reasonable reinvestigation. Disputing with us
and with the agency are independent routes and may be used together; neither route requires payment of any fee, and no service can lawfully remove
information that is accurate and current.

3. Circumstances Requiring Coverage
Where the improvements securing the loan are located in a special flood hazard area and the community participates in the National Flood Insurance Program,
federal law prohibits the extension of credit unless flood insurance is obtained for the term of the loan. Evidence of coverage must be provided before closing,
and the coverage must remain in force continuously thereafter.

Where the community does not participate in the program, federally backed coverage is unavailable, and the loan may be subject to program restrictions or to
a requirement of private coverage. The consequences of nonparticipation, including the unavailability of federal disaster assistance for certain purposes, are
described in the notice accompanying the determination form.

4. Use of Vendors and Agents
We engage third parties to perform functions in connection with the origination and servicing of residential mortgage loans, including document preparation,
data processing, payment processing, tax and flood determination services, insurance tracking, appraisal management, printing, and mailing. Those providers
receive only the information necessary to perform the service for which they are engaged.

Each provider is bound by contract to maintain the confidentiality and security of the information disclosed to it and to use that information only for the purposes
of the engagement. Engaging a service provider does not relieve us of responsibility for the performance of the function delegated, and inquiries concerning
any such function may be directed to us rather than to the provider.

5. Required Coverage Amounts
The minimum amount of flood insurance required is the least of the outstanding principal balance of the loan, the maximum limit of coverage available for the
property type under the National Flood Insurance Program, or the insurable value of the improvements. Insurable value is generally measured by replacement
cost, or by another method appropriate to the property, and excludes the value of the land.

Contents coverage is not required by the lender and does not satisfy the building-coverage requirement, although you may find it valuable. Where the property
is a unit in a condominium or association covered by a master flood policy, the association's coverage may satisfy part or all of the requirement; evidence of the
master policy and of the allocation applicable to the unit is required.

6. Escrow of Flood Premiums
Federal law requires that premiums for flood insurance be escrowed for most residential loans secured by property in a special flood hazard area, subject to
limited exceptions for small institutions and for certain loan types. Where escrow applies, the premium is collected monthly with your payment and disbursed by
the servicer when the policy renews.




                                                              Retain this document with your loan file records.                                            Page 1 of 3
Where escrow is not required at origination, you may nonetheless be offered the option to escrow, and in certain circumstances the servicer is required to offer
it later. The escrow disclosure furnished to you separately describes how the account is established, analyzed annually, and adjusted for changes in the
premium.

7. Language Assistance
This document is provided in English. If English is not your primary language, you may wish to have it reviewed with the assistance of a translator or an adviser
of your choosing before you rely upon it. Where we make a translated version of a document available, the translation is furnished as a courtesy; unless
applicable law provides otherwise, the English version governs the rights and obligations of the parties.

Free language assistance is available through the housing counseling organizations identified in the notice furnished to you concerning the availability of
counseling, many of which offer services in multiple languages. If you require assistance in communicating with us about loan number 1234567890, call (555)
555-0120 and identify the language you prefer so that we may make appropriate arrangements.

8. Failure to Maintain Coverage
If required flood coverage lapses or is found to be insufficient, the servicer must notify you and, if acceptable coverage is not obtained within forty-five (45) days
of that notice, must purchase coverage on your behalf and charge the premium and any related fees to your account. Coverage purchased in that manner
protects the lender's interest and is ordinarily more expensive than a policy you obtain yourself.

Where you subsequently provide evidence that acceptable coverage was in force during a period for which lender-purchased coverage was charged, the
overlapping premium and fees are refunded and the account is adjusted. The most effective protection is simply to renew your policy on time and to send the
declarations page to the servicer at each renewal.

9. Reservation of Rights
No failure or delay on our part in exercising any right, power, or privilege under the loan documents operates as a waiver of it, and no single or partial exercise
of any right precludes a further exercise of that right or the exercise of any other. Any waiver must be in writing and signed by an authorized officer of ABC
Mortgage Company to be effective, and it extends only to the specific matter identified in it.

Our rights and remedies are cumulative and may be exercised concurrently, successively, or in any order. Nothing in this document creates any right in favor of
a third party, and no course of dealing between you and us, and no accommodation extended on one occasion, varies the written terms of the loan documents
or establishes a practice on which either party may rely thereafter.

Correspondingly, nothing in this document waives, limits, or diminishes any right, protection, or remedy available to you under federal law or under the law of
NY. To the extent any provision of this document is inconsistent with such a right, the right controls and the remaining provisions continue in effect.

10. Changes to This Document
We may revise this document from time to time to reflect changes in applicable law, in regulatory guidance, or in our own procedures. Where a revision
materially affects your rights or obligations, we will furnish a revised document or a notice describing the change in the manner and within the time that
applicable law requires, and the revision will apply prospectively from its stated effective date.

A revision does not alter the note, the security instrument, or the payment terms to which you agreed, none of which may be changed except as those
documents expressly permit or by a written modification executed by you and by an authorized officer. The version of this document currently in effect may be
requested at any time from ABC Mortgage Company at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY 12345.

11. Federal Disaster Assistance
Federal disaster assistance is available only where a disaster is formally declared by the President, and it typically takes the form of a loan that must be repaid
with interest rather than a grant covering the loss. Assistance is often limited relative to the cost of repairing flood damage, and it is not a substitute for
insurance.

Where a property in a special flood hazard area has previously received federal disaster assistance conditioned upon maintaining flood insurance, and
coverage was not maintained, future assistance for that property may be denied by operation of law. That consequence follows the property and may affect a
subsequent owner.

12. Complaints and Escalation
If you are dissatisfied with any aspect of the handling of loan number 1234567890, we ask that you first raise the matter with us by telephone at (555)
555-0120 or in writing at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY 12345, describing the issue, the dates and amounts involved, and the resolution you seek. Most
concerns are resolved fastest at that level, and a written summary from you is the most reliable way to ensure the matter is understood as you intend it.

You may also, at any time and without first contacting us, submit a complaint to the federal consumer complaint system, to the state regulator having
jurisdiction over the institution in NY, or to the federal banking agency that supervises us. Raising a concern with us does not waive, shorten, or otherwise limit
any right you have to pursue the matter with a regulator or through any other remedy available at law or in equity.

13. Questions About This Notice
Questions concerning the determination, the amount of coverage required, or the escrow of flood premiums for loan number 1234567890 may be directed to
ABC Mortgage Company at (555) 555-0120 or at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY 12345. Questions concerning the flood maps themselves, the letter of map
amendment process, or the terms of a federal policy should be directed to your insurance agent or to the Federal Emergency Management Agency.

This notice is provided as of November 14, 2024 and summarizes federal requirements applicable to property located in NY. Where this summary differs from
the governing statute or regulation, or from the Standard Flood Hazard Determination Form completed for this transaction, those documents control.

14. Consent to Verify
You authorize ABC Mortgage Company, and any assignee or servicer of loan number 1234567890, to verify the information you have provided in connection
with the transaction, including by obtaining consumer reports, verifying employment and income, confirming deposit and asset balances with the institutions
holding them, obtaining tax return transcripts where you have executed the applicable authorization, and confirming the existence and terms of insurance
coverage on the property.

Verification may occur at any time during the origination of the credit and again before closing, and information obtained through verification is used in
evaluating the credit request and in servicing the account thereafter. Information collected in this manner is handled in accordance with the privacy notice
furnished to you and with applicable federal and NY law.

15. Reading the Determination Form
The Standard Flood Hazard Determination Form identifies the lender, the borrower, and the property; states the community name and identifier; gives the map
panel number and its effective date; and records whether the improvements are in a special flood hazard area and whether the community participates in the
federal program. Review each field against the property you are financing.

The determination applies to the improvements rather than to the parcel as a whole. A property whose lot is partly within a mapped flood zone but whose
dwelling is outside it is not subject to the mandatory purchase requirement, which is one reason the location of the structure matters more than the boundary
drawn across the land.

16. Fraud Awareness and Reporting
Mortgage transactions attract fraud, most commonly in the form of messages that appear to come from a lender, a settlement agent, or a real estate
professional and that direct funds to an account controlled by a criminal. We do not transmit wiring instructions by electronic message, and we do not change
previously issued remittance instructions by electronic message. Verify any such instruction by telephone at a number you have independently confirmed
before transferring funds.

Report a suspicious communication concerning loan number 1234567890 to us at (555) 555-0120 promptly, and preserve the message rather than deleting it.
If funds have already been transmitted, contact your financial institution immediately and ask that a recall be initiated; the prospects of recovery diminish
sharply within hours, and prompt action is by far the most important factor.

17. Cost of Coverage and Elevation
Premiums under the federal program reflect the flood risk of the structure, including its elevation relative to the base flood elevation, its foundation type, and the
location of its lowest floor and machinery. An elevation certificate prepared by a licensed surveyor documents those characteristics and may materially affect
the premium.

Coverage is also available in zones outside the special flood hazard area, frequently at a lower premium, and a substantial share of flood claims arise from
properties outside mapped high-risk zones. Standard homeowners policies exclude flood damage, so the absence of a federal requirement is not a reason to
assume the risk is covered elsewhere.

18. Private Flood Insurance
Coverage from a private carrier may be accepted in satisfaction of the mandatory purchase requirement where it meets the definition of private flood insurance
established by federal regulation, or where it satisfies the discretionary acceptance criteria that permit a lender to accept a policy providing sufficient protection
consistent with safety and soundness.

If you wish to place coverage privately, provide the policy or binder early so that acceptability can be confirmed before closing. Private coverage may offer
higher limits or broader terms than the federal program, and it may also carry different renewal and cancellation practices; compare the policies rather than the
premiums alone.

Your Credit Score and the Information Used to Obtain It
ABC MORTGAGE COMPANY — YOUR CREDIT SCORE AND THE INFORMATION USED TO OBTAIN IT
Loan #1234567890 · ABC Mortgage Company · 11/21/2024
Document LN-3603 · Rev. 5.7 · In effect as of 10/28/2022



If any part of this document is unclear to you, contact us before you sign or rely upon it. In connection with your application for a loan secured by one to
four units of residential real property, ABC Mortgage Company is required to disclose to John Doe the credit score or scores obtained from consumer
reporting agencies and used in connection with the application identified as loan number 1234567890. The scores, the range of possible scores, the key
factors reported as adversely affecting each score, and the identity of the agency that supplied it appear on the accompanying score-disclosure page.
This notice explains what a credit score is, how it is used, and the rights you have with respect to the underlying consumer reports as of November 14,
2024.

Section 1. Understanding Your Score
A credit score is a computer-generated number that summarizes your credit record at a point in time and estimates the relative likelihood that an obligation will
be repaid as agreed. Scores are calculated by, or on behalf of, consumer reporting agencies using statistical models applied to the information in the file that
the agency maintains about you. They are not calculated by ABC Mortgage Company.

Because each agency maintains its own file, and because several scoring models are in commercial use, the score obtained from one agency may differ from
the score obtained from another on the same day, and a score obtained under a mortgage model may differ from a score you have seen through a consumer-
facing service. A difference between such figures does not by itself indicate that any file is inaccurate.

Section 2. The Role of Scores in Underwriting
Credit scores are one of several factors considered in a mortgage credit decision. Underwriting also weighs income and its stability, the ratio of housing and
total obligations to income, the funds available for the transaction and for reserves, the value and condition of the collateral, and the requirements of the loan
program and of any investor or insurer. A score is a summary indicator, not the decision itself.

Scores may also affect the pricing of credit. Where a loan program applies price adjustments based on the combination of credit score and loan-to-value ratio,
those adjustments are reflected in the interest rate or in the charges disclosed on your Loan Estimate and Closing Disclosure. The composition of your rate is
disclosed on those documents rather than in this notice.

Section 3. Joint Borrowers and Multiple Obligors
Where more than one person is obligated on loan number 1234567890, each of you is jointly and severally liable for the entire obligation. That means the full
amount may be enforced against any one of you, against some of you, or against all of you together, without any requirement that other obligors, guarantors, or
collateral be pursued first, and a release or accommodation extended to one of you does not impair the liability of the others.

Any communication we deliver to one of you is treated as delivered to all of you, and an instruction, election, or authorization given by one of you may be acted
upon as though given by all of you unless the loan documents or applicable law require otherwise. Where your instructions conflict, we may decline to act until
the conflict is resolved among you in writing.

A change in the relationship among obligors — including a separation, a divorce, a transfer of an interest in the property, or the death of a borrower — does not
by itself alter the obligation or release any person from it. Notify us of such an event so that our records reflect the correct parties, and consult your own
attorney concerning the effect of the event on the ownership of 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345.

Section 4. Key Factors Affecting Your Score
The score-disclosure page accompanying this notice lists the key factors that adversely affected each score, in order of importance, as reported by the agency
that produced it. Common factors include the presence of derogatory information, the length of time accounts have been established, the proportion of
revolving balances to available credit limits, the number of recent inquiries, and the mix of account types in the file.

These factors are generated by the scoring model, not by ABC Mortgage Company, and we cannot alter them or recompute a score. A factor is a description of
what most influenced the number on the date it was calculated; it does not necessarily identify anything improper in the file, and a factor may appear even
where the score is high.

Section 5. Effect of a Transfer of Servicing
The servicing of loan number 1234567890 — the collection of payments, the administration of any escrow account, and the handling of your inquiries — may
be transferred to another company at any time. A transfer of servicing is not a sale of your obligation to a different borrower and does not change the interest
rate, the payment amount, the maturity date, or any other term of the note or the security instrument.

Where servicing transfers, you receive a notice from the transferor at least fifteen (15) days before the effective date and a notice from the transferee within
fifteen (15) days after it, unless the transfer occurs in circumstances for which the law permits a combined or later notice. The notices identify both companies,
the date payments should begin going to the new servicer, and the telephone numbers at which each may be reached.

For sixty (60) days after the effective date of a transfer, a payment received by the prior servicer on or before its due date may not be treated as late merely
because it was sent to the wrong company. Even so, redirect your payments promptly, and update any automatic payment arrangement you maintain through
your own financial institution, since that arrangement is under your control rather than ours.




                                                             Retain this document with your loan file records.                                           Page 1 of 3
Section 6. Defined Terms
Unless the context plainly requires otherwise, "you" and "your" refer to John Doe and to any other person obligated on loan number 1234567890; "we," "us,"
and "our" refer to ABC Mortgage Company and to any successor, assignee, or servicer that acquires the loan or the right to service it; and "the property" refers
to the real property located at 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345 that secures the loan. "Applicable law" means the federal statutes and regulations
governing residential mortgage credit together with the law of the State of NY, in each case as amended from time to time.

"Business day" carries the meaning given to it by the particular statute or regulation under which a right or deadline arises, and the count therefore differs
among the documents furnished to you; where a specific count matters, it is stated in the section that establishes the deadline. "Loan documents" means the
note, the security instrument, and every rider, addendum, disclosure, and agreement executed or delivered in connection with the credit transaction described
above.

Section 7. Relationship to Your Other Loan Documents
This document supplements the note, the security instrument, and the disclosures furnished to you in connection with loan number 1234567890. It does not
enlarge, reduce, or otherwise modify the amounts payable, the interest rate, the payment schedule, or any right or remedy established by those instruments,
and no statement here should be read as a representation that any particular term applies to your transaction.

Where this document summarizes a statute, a regulation, or a program requirement, the summary is provided for convenience. In the event of any difference
between the summary and the authority summarized, the statute, regulation, or program requirement controls, and no summary in this document limits any
right afforded to you by law.

Section 8. Obtaining Your Consumer Report
You have the right to obtain a copy of the consumer report from any agency that furnished one in connection with this application. Under federal law you are
entitled to a free copy of your report from each nationwide agency at least once every twelve months, and you may obtain additional free copies in
circumstances the statute defines, including where adverse action is taken on the basis of information in the report.

Reviewing your report periodically is the most effective way to confirm that the information about you is accurate and complete. The report contains the
underlying account and public-record data; the score is a derived figure. Correcting an inaccuracy in the underlying data is what causes a score to change.

Section 9. Correcting Information in Your Report
If you believe that information in a consumer report is inaccurate or incomplete, you may dispute it with the consumer reporting agency that issued the report
and with the furnisher of the information. The agency must generally conduct a reasonable reinvestigation, ordinarily within thirty (30) days, and must delete or
correct information it finds to be inaccurate, incomplete, or unverifiable.

Disputes should be submitted directly to the agency, in writing where possible, and should identify the item disputed and the reason. Include copies rather than
originals of any supporting documents. ABC Mortgage Company did not create the information in your report and cannot correct it, although we will consider a
corrected report or a supplemental verification you provide during the underwriting of loan number 1234567890.

Section 10. Agencies Are Not the Decision-Maker
The consumer reporting agencies that supplied the reports and scores played no part in the decision on your application and are unable to explain why any
decision was made. Questions about the disposition of your application, about the terms offered, or about the conditions of an approval should be directed to
ABC Mortgage Company at (555) 555-0120.

If adverse action is taken in whole or in part on the basis of information contained in a consumer report, you will receive a separate notice identifying the
agency, stating that the agency did not make the decision, and describing your right to obtain a free copy of the report and to dispute its contents within the
periods the statute prescribes.

Section 11. Scores in Joint Applications
Where more than one applicant is obligated on the loan, scores are obtained for each applicant, and each applicant receives this notice together with the
scores associated with that applicant. Underwriting guidelines determine which score among several is used for qualification and pricing; the rule applied varies
among loan programs and investors.

The disclosure of one applicant's scores to another is limited by privacy law and by the terms of the authorization each applicant provided. Each applicant may
obtain his or her own reports directly from the agencies at any time using the process described above.

Section 12. Computation of Time Periods
Unless a particular statute, regulation, or provision states otherwise, a period expressed in days is measured in calendar days, the day of the act or event that
starts the period is excluded, and the last day is included. Where the last day falls on a Saturday, a Sunday, or a legal public holiday, the period runs to the end
of the next day that is not one of those days.

Several requirements applicable to residential mortgage transactions are measured in business days, and the definition of a business day differs among them:
one rule counts days on which our offices are open for substantially all business, while another counts all calendar days except Sundays and legal public
holidays. Where a specific count controls a right or a deadline, it is stated in the provision that establishes it.

Where a period is measured from the delivery of a document, delivery by mail is generally presumed to occur three business days after mailing unless earlier
receipt is documented. Because these conventions determine real deadlines in your transaction, confirm the applicable dates with us or with your settlement
agent rather than estimating them.

Section 13. Improving a Score Over Time
Scores respond over time to the payment and balance behavior recorded in the underlying file. Paying every obligation as agreed, keeping revolving balances
well below the available limit, allowing established accounts to remain open, and limiting new applications to those actually needed are the behaviors that
scoring models generally reward. No service can lawfully remove accurate, current information from a report.

Be cautious of any organization that offers, for a fee, to create a new credit identity, to remove accurate information, or to guarantee a specific score increase.
Such offers are frequently unlawful and may expose you to liability. Free assistance with credit questions is available from the homeownership counseling
organizations identified in the separate notice furnished to you.

Section 14. Recordkeeping and Questions
Retain this notice and the accompanying score-disclosure page with your loan records. The scores shown are those obtained in connection with this
application on the dates indicated, and they are not updated after that date. A later score obtained for another purpose will differ and does not supersede what
is disclosed here.

agreement between you and ABC Mortgage Company.

Section 15. How to Contact Us
General questions concerning loan number 1234567890 may be directed to ABC Mortgage Company by telephone at (555) 555-0120 during normal business
hours, or in writing at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY 12345. Please reference the loan number and the property address in every written communication so that
your correspondence is matched to the correct file without delay, and retain a copy of anything you send together with a note of the date it was sent.

Certain submissions must be sent to a specific designated address in order to receive the treatment that law prescribes, including a written notice of asserted
error, a request for information, and a request to exercise a privacy election. Where a designated address applies, it is identified on your periodic statement and
in the corresponding notice; using the general correspondence address for such a submission may result in a slower response.

Section 16. Inquiries and Rate Shopping
An inquiry recorded when a creditor obtains your report in connection with an application may affect a score modestly. Scoring models used for mortgage
lending generally treat multiple mortgage inquiries occurring within a defined shopping window as a single inquiry, so comparing offers among several lenders
within a short period does not compound the effect.

A request you make for your own report, and a promotional or account-review inquiry made without your application, are not treated as inquiries by scoring
models. Comparison shopping is therefore not penalized in the way consumers frequently fear, and it remains the most effective means of evaluating the cost
of credit.

Section 17. Reissued and Updated Reports
A consumer report obtained at application has a limited useful life, and a program or investor may require that it be updated or reissued before closing,
particularly where the transaction is delayed. An updated report may show new activity, and a material change may require the file to be reviewed again before
the transaction proceeds.

For that reason, avoid opening new accounts, financing furniture or a vehicle, or closing established accounts between application and closing on loan number
1234567890. Discuss any planned change in your credit obligations with us first, so that its effect on qualification can be evaluated before it occurs rather than
discovered at the closing table.

§ 1. Scope of This Document

without impairment.

Each section below addresses a separate subject matter and may be relied upon independently. The headings are provided solely for convenience and ease of
reference and do not limit, expand, or otherwise affect the substance of the acknowledgments that follow. John Doe understands that signing this document
does not obligate ABC Mortgage Company to close or fund the loan and does not waive any condition that ABC Mortgage Company may impose prior to
closing. Nothing herein creates any commitment except as expressly stated in a separately executed written commitment from ABC Mortgage Company.

John Doe acknowledges that this document has been made available in a manner permitting review prior to execution, and that John Doe has had a
reasonable opportunity to read it, to ask questions of ABC Mortgage Company, and to seek independent advice from counsel or other advisors of John Doe's
choosing. The execution of this document reflects John Doe's informed and voluntary agreement to the matters described herein as of the date set forth above.

§ 2. Occupancy Certification
John Doe certifies the intended occupancy status of the subject property located at 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345 as represented in the loan
application. If the property has been represented as John Doe's principal residence, John Doe certifies an intention to occupy, establish, and use the property
as John Doe's principal residence within the period customarily required following closing, and to continue to occupy the property as a principal residence for
the period required by the loan documents, unless otherwise agreed by ABC Mortgage Company in writing or required by extenuating circumstances beyond
John Doe's reasonable control.

John Doe understands that the occupancy representation is a material factor in ABC Mortgage Company's underwriting decision and in the pricing and terms of
the loan, and that loans secured by a principal residence may carry different terms than loans secured by second homes or investment properties. John Doe

  This report form is designed to report an appraisal of a one-unit property or a one-unit property with an accessory unit; including a unit in a planned unit development
  (PUD). This report form is not designed to report an appraisal of a manufactured home or a unit in a condominium or cooperative project.

  This appraisal report is subject to the following scope of work, intended use, intended user, definition of market value, statement of assumptions and limiting conditions,
  and certifications. Modifications, additions, or deletions to the intended use, intended user, definition of market value, or assumptions and limiting conditions are not
  permitted. The appraiser may expand the scope of work to include any additional research or analysis necessary based on the complexity of this appraisal assignment.
  Modifications or deletions to the certifications are also not permitted. However, additional certifications that do not constitute material alterations to this appraisal report,
  such as those required by law or those related to the appraiser's continuing education or membership in an appraisal organization, are permitted.

  SCOPE OF WORK: The scope of work for this appraisal is defined by the complexity of this appraisal assignment and the reporting requirements of this appraisal report
  form, including the following definition of market value, statement of assumptions and limiting conditions, and certifications. The appraiser must, at a minimum: (1) perform
  a complete visual inspection of the interior and exterior areas of the subject property, (2) inspect the neighborhood, (3) inspect each of the comparable sales from at least
  the street, (4) research, verify, and analyze data from reliable public and/or private sources, and (5) report his or her analysis, opinions, and conclusions in this appraisal
  report.

  INTENDED USE: The intended use of this appraisal report is for the lender/client to evaluate the property that is the subject of this appraisal for a mortgage finance
  transaction.

  INTENDED USER: The intended user of this appraisal report is the lender/client.

  DEFINITION OF MARKET VALUE: The most probable price which a property should bring in a competitive and open market under all conditions requisite to a fair sale,
  the buyer and seller each acting prudently, knowledgeably and assuming the price is not affected by undue stimulus. Implicit in this definition is the consummation of a sale
  as of a specified date and the passing of title from seller to buyer under conditions whereby: (1) buyer and seller are typically motivated; (2) both parties are well informed
  or well advised, and each acting in what he or she considers his or her own best interest; (3) a reasonable time is allowed for exposure in the open market; (4) payment is
  made in terms of cash in U.S. dollars or in terms of financial arrangements comparable thereto; and (5) the price represents the normal consideration for the property sold
  unaffected by special or creative financing or sales concessions granted by anyone associated with the sale.

  *Adjustments to the comparables must be made for special or creative financing or sales concessions. No adjustments are necessary for those costs which are normally
  paid by sellers as a result of tradition or law in a market area; these costs are readily identifiable since the seller pays these costs in virtually all sales transactions. Special
  or creative financing adjustments can be made to the comparable property by comparisons to financing terms offered by a third party institutional lender that is not already
  involved in the property or transaction. Any adjustment should not be calculated on a mechanical dollar for dollar cost of the financing or concession but the dollar amount
  of any adjustment should approximate the market's reaction to the financing or concessions based on the appraiser's judgment.

  STATEMENT OF ASSUMPTIONS AND LIMITING CONDITIONS: The appraiser's certification in this report is subject to the following assumptions and limiting conditions:

  1. The appraiser will not be responsible for matters of a legal nature that affect either the property being appraised or the title to it, except for information that the appraiser
  became aware of during the research involved in performing this appraisal. The appraiser assumes that the title is good and marketable and will not render any opinions
  about the title.

  2. The appraiser has examined the available flood maps that are provided by the Federal Emergency Management Agency and has noted in this appraisal report whether
  any portion of the subject site is located in an identified Special Flood Hazard Area. The appraiser is not a surveyor and makes no guarantees, express or implied,
  regarding this determination.

  3. The appraiser will not give testimony or appear in court because he or she made an appraisal of the property in question, unless specific arrangements to do so have
  been made beforehand, or as otherwise required by law.

  4. The appraiser has noted in this appraisal report any adverse conditions such as needed repairs, deterioration, the presence of hazardous wastes, toxic substances, etc.
  observed during the inspection of the subject property, or that he or she became aware of during the research involved in performing this appraisal. Unless otherwise
  stated in this appraisal report, the appraiser has no knowledge of any hidden or unapparent physical deficiencies of the property.

  5. The appraiser obtained the information, estimates and opinions that were expressed in this appraisal report from sources believed to be reliable and believes them to be
  true and correct. The appraiser does not assume responsibility for the accuracy of such items that were furnished by other parties.

  6. The appraiser will not disclose the contents of this appraisal report except as provided for in the Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice and any applicable
  federal, state or local laws.

  7. The appraiser has based his or her appraisal report and valuation conclusion for an appraisal that is subject to satisfactory completion, repairs, or alterations on the
  assumption that the completion, repairs, or alterations of the subject property will be performed in a professional manner.

Scope of Work

 The scope of work for this assignment was determined by the intended use of the report — a purchase-money mortgage finance transaction — and the intended user, ABC
 Mortgage Company. The appraiser inspected the interior and exterior of the subject on 11/02/2024, measured the improvements, photographed the subject and each
 comparable from the street, and researched the multiple listing service, county public records and the contract of sale. Comparable sales were selected from the subject
 neighborhood and analyzed on a price-per-unit and paired-sales basis. The sales comparison approach was developed; the cost and income approaches were not necessary
 for credible assignment results and were not developed.

Highest and Best Use

 The subject is a one-unit dwelling on a 0.25 acres site zoned R-1 Single Family Residential. The present use is legal and conforming, is physically possible, financially feasible
 and maximally productive; the highest and best use as improved is therefore the present residential use. No alternative use would produce a greater return to the site.

Comparable Selection and Adjustment Support

 The comparable sales are the most recent closed sales of similar one-unit dwellings located within one-half mile of the subject. All are in the subject neighborhood, are of similar
 site size, design, quality and age, and required no adjustment for location, view, leasehold interest, room count or functional utility. Adjustments were limited to gross living area
 at a market-supported rate, market conditions measured from the date of each sale, and amenity differences. Gross adjustments are within accepted guidelines and the
 adjusted values bracket and support the opinion of value.

A copy of this document is retained in the file maintained for loan number 1234567890. This policy explains how payments received on loan number
1234567890 are applied, what happens when an amount received is less than a full contractual payment, how funds held in suspense are treated, and
how you may direct an additional amount toward principal. The partial payment policy applicable to your loan is also stated on your Closing Disclosure,
and the entry on that document controls in the event of any difference. This statement is furnished for your convenience so that the treatment of every
payment you make on the property at 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345 is clear from the outset.

Article I. What Constitutes a Full Payment
A full contractual payment consists of the scheduled principal and interest, plus the monthly escrow deposit where an escrow account is maintained, plus any
other recurring amount identified on your periodic statement, such as an optional product premium you have elected. The total appears on your billing
statement as the amount due. Any remittance below that total is a partial payment regardless of how close it comes to the amount due.

Amounts past due from a prior period are added to the current amount due. Where more than one payment is outstanding, the total due reflects each unpaid
installment together with any late charge properly assessed, and a remittance sufficient to cover only one installment is applied to the oldest outstanding
installment first.

Article II. Relationship to Your Other Loan Documents
This document supplements the note, the security instrument, and the disclosures furnished to you in connection with loan number 1234567890. It does not
enlarge, reduce, or otherwise modify the amounts payable, the interest rate, the payment schedule, or any right or remedy established by those instruments,
and no statement here should be read as a representation that any particular term applies to your transaction.

Where this document summarizes a statute, a regulation, or a program requirement, the summary is provided for convenience. In the event of any difference
between the summary and the authority summarized, the statute, regulation, or program requirement controls, and no summary in this document limits any
right afforded to you by law.

Article III. Order in Which Payments Are Applied
Unless applicable law or the terms of your note require otherwise, a payment received and accepted is applied first to accrued interest, then to principal, then
to the escrow deposit, then to any late charges outstanding, and finally to other fees and advances properly assessed against the account. This is the order
used for every regular monthly payment and is not varied at the election of the servicer.

The order of application governs the composition of the payment, not whether the payment satisfies the obligation. A payment applied in this order still leaves
the installment unpaid if the total remitted is less than the amount due, and the account is reported as it actually stands after application.

Article IV. Partial Payments and Suspense
Where the servicer accepts a partial payment, the funds are ordinarily placed in a suspense or unapplied-funds account rather than applied immediately to the
loan. Funds remain in suspense until enough has accumulated to make a full contractual payment, at which point the full amount is applied in the standard
order and credited as of the date the account reached that total.

Funds held in suspense do not reduce the principal balance and do not stop the accrual of interest. Your periodic statement identifies any amount held in
suspense so that the status of the account is visible to you. If you prefer that a partial remittance be returned rather than held, notify the servicer at (555)
555-0120 at the time the payment is made.

Article V. Successors and Assigns
We may sell, assign, transfer, pledge, or otherwise convey the loan, the loan documents, or the right to service the loan, in whole or in part, at any time and
without your consent, except as applicable law requires. A transfer of ownership or of servicing does not by itself change the interest rate, the payment amount,
the maturity date, or any other term of your obligation, and the transferee succeeds to the rights and, to the extent of the transfer, the obligations described in
the loan documents.

This document binds and benefits you and us and our respective heirs, executors, administrators, successors, and permitted assigns. You may not assign or
delegate your rights or obligations without our prior written consent, and the sale or transfer of the property at 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345 does not
release you from liability for the debt unless we expressly agree in writing to a release.

Article VI. Extra Principal Payments
You may pay more than the amount due at any time. To ensure that the extra amount is applied to principal rather than held for the next installment, indicate
the additional principal amount on the coupon or in the designated field of the online payment screen, or include a written instruction identifying the amount and
referencing loan number 1234567890. An unmarked overpayment may be held toward the next scheduled installment.

An additional principal payment reduces the outstanding balance and the total interest paid over the life of the loan, but it does not change the amount or the
due date of the next scheduled payment unless your note expressly provides otherwise. Continue to make each regular monthly payment in full after making
an additional principal payment.

Article VII. Identity Verification Requirements
Federal law requires all financial institutions to obtain, verify, and record information identifying each person who opens an account, in order to help the
government fight the funding of terrorism and money-laundering activities. When you apply for credit, we ask for your name, address, date of birth, and other
information that allows us to identify you, and we may ask to see a driver's license or other identifying document.

The information collected for this purpose is used to verify identity and is retained in accordance with applicable law. It is not used as a factor in evaluating
creditworthiness, and requesting identifying documentation is a routine step applied to every applicant rather than an indication of any concern about a
particular transaction.

Article VIII. Payment Methods and Crediting
Payments may be made by mail to the remittance address shown on your statement, by automatic monthly debit, by single online payment, or by telephone
where that service is offered. A payment received in the manner and at the location specified on your statement on or before the due date is credited as of the
date of receipt, even if the servicer's internal processing is completed on a later date.

A payment made by an unauthorized method, sent to an incorrect address, or tendered without sufficient identifying information may be delayed. Where a
payment cannot be identified, the servicer attempts to locate the account and, failing that, returns the funds to the sender. Always include the loan number on
any check or money order.

Article IX. Amendments and Future Revisions
We may revise this document from time to time to reflect changes in applicable law, in regulatory guidance, or in our own procedures. Where a revision
materially affects your rights or obligations, we will furnish a revised document or a notice describing the change in the manner and within the time that
applicable law requires, and the revision will apply prospectively from its stated effective date.

A revision does not alter the note, the security instrument, or the payment terms to which you agreed, none of which may be changed except as those
documents expressly permit or by a written modification executed by you and by an authorized officer. The version of this document currently in effect may be
requested at any time from ABC Mortgage Company at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY 12345.

Article X. Consent to Verify
You authorize ABC Mortgage Company, and any assignee or servicer of loan number 1234567890, to verify the information you have provided in connection
with the transaction, including by obtaining consumer reports, verifying employment and income, confirming deposit and asset balances with the institutions
holding them, obtaining tax return transcripts where you have executed the applicable authorization, and confirming the existence and terms of insurance
coverage on the property.

Verification may occur at any time during the origination of the credit and again before closing, and information obtained through verification is used in
evaluating the credit request and in servicing the account thereafter. Information collected in this manner is handled in accordance with the privacy notice
furnished to you and with applicable federal and NY law.

Article XI. Late Charges and Returned Items
If a check, draft, or electronic transfer is returned unpaid for any reason, the credit previously given is reversed, the payment is treated as never having been
made, and a returned-item fee is assessed where permitted by law and the loan documents. After a returned item, the servicer may require that subsequent
payments be made in certified funds for a period.

A late charge is assessed when a payment is not received in full by the end of the grace period stated in your note. The charge compensates for the
administrative cost of handling a delinquent payment; it is not interest, not a penalty, and not consent to late payment. A late charge is never assessed on a
payment received in full and on time, and a charge assessed in error is reversed upon review.

Article XII. Computation of Time Periods
Unless a particular statute, regulation, or provision states otherwise, a period expressed in days is measured in calendar days, the day of the act or event that
starts the period is excluded, and the last day is included. Where the last day falls on a Saturday, a Sunday, or a legal public holiday, the period runs to the end
of the next day that is not one of those days.

Several requirements applicable to residential mortgage transactions are measured in business days, and the definition of a business day differs among them:
one rule counts days on which our offices are open for substantially all business, while another counts all calendar days except Sundays and legal public
holidays. Where a specific count controls a right or a deadline, it is stated in the provision that establishes it.

Where a period is measured from the delivery of a document, delivery by mail is generally presumed to occur three business days after mailing unless earlier
receipt is documented. Because these conventions determine real deadlines in your transaction, confirm the applicable dates with us or with your settlement
agent rather than estimating them.

Article XIII. Suspense Balances and Payoff
When the loan is paid in full, any amount remaining in suspense is applied to the payoff or refunded to you, and the payoff statement identifies how a suspense
balance is being treated. A suspense balance is not automatically deducted from the payoff figure quoted to a third party, so the settlement agent should
confirm the treatment before disbursing funds.

If servicing is transferred, funds held in suspense transfer with the loan and continue to be held under the same terms by the transferee servicer. The transfer
notice furnished to you identifies the date after which payments should be sent to the new servicer.

Article XIV. If You Believe a Payment Was Misapplied
If you believe a payment was misapplied, held in suspense in error, or credited on an incorrect date, contact the servicer at (555) 555-0120 or submit a written
notice of error to 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY 12345. A written notice invokes the error-resolution procedures described in the separate notice furnished to
you, which require an acknowledgment and a substantive response within defined periods.

This policy is provided as of November 14, 2024 and applies to loan number 1234567890 until superseded. It summarizes the payment terms of your loan
documents; in the event of a conflict, the note, the security instrument, and the partial payment entry on your Closing Disclosure control.

Article XV. Updating Your Contact Information
Notify us promptly of any change in your mailing address, telephone number, or electronic address, and of any change in the name in which the account is
held. Until we have received notice of a change and have had a reasonable opportunity to act upon it, we are entitled to rely on the information most recently
reflected in our records, and a communication sent to that information remains effective.

Keeping your information current matters most at exactly the moments it is easiest to overlook: after a move, after a change in marital status, after a change in
electronic mail provider, and after the transfer of servicing. Several of the notices described in the documents furnished to you carry response deadlines, and a
notice that does not reach you still starts the period it establishes.

Article XVI. Automatic Payment Arrangements
Where you authorize an automatic monthly debit, the amount debited is the total then due, and it changes when your escrow analysis changes the payment.
Confirm the amount of the first debit after any analysis so that the change is expected. You may cancel or modify the authorization by notifying us within the
period stated in the authorization, generally at least three business days before the scheduled date.

An arrangement you establish through your own bank's bill-payment service is under your control rather than ours; we can neither change nor cancel it. If the
payment amount changes, update that arrangement yourself, because a bill-payment service continues to send the former amount indefinitely, producing a
small shortfall each month that eventually accumulates into a missed installment.

Article XVII. Payments From Third Parties
We may accept a payment tendered by a person other than a borrower, such as a family member or a settlement agent, and acceptance of such a payment
does not make that person liable on the loan, does not confer any right to information about the account, and does not create any relationship between that
person and ABC Mortgage Company beyond the transaction itself.

Information about loan number 1234567890 is released only to a borrower or to a person you have authorized in writing. A third party who remits a payment
and then wishes to confirm its application must be authorized by you, and we will explain the authorization process to that person without disclosing account
information in the meantime.

Article XVIII. Biweekly and Accelerated Payment Plans
Some borrowers arrange to pay half of a monthly payment every two weeks, which produces one additional monthly payment each year and shortens the term.
Where we offer such a plan, its terms, including when funds are applied and whether a fee applies, are stated in the plan agreement. Funds under such a plan
are ordinarily held until a full contractual payment is available and then applied.

The same result can be achieved without a plan and without a fee by adding an amount equal to one-twelfth of a monthly payment to each regular payment
and designating it as additional principal. Third-party services that offer to administer accelerated payments for a fee provide no benefit that you cannot obtain
directly, and they insert an intermediary between you and the servicer.

in Schedule A, and will include the following Exceptions from Coverage unless each is disposed of to the Company’s

Borrower Duties for Property Charges
ABC MORTGAGE COMPANY — PROPERTY TAX AND INSURANCE RESPONSIBILITIES
Loan #1234567890 · ABC Mortgage Company · 11/17/2024
Document LN-4699 · Rev. 3.1 · In effect as of 06/23/2024



This notice summarizes the obligations of John Doe with respect to property taxes, assessments, and insurance coverage on the property located at
456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345, which secures loan number 1234567890. These obligations continue for the entire term of the loan and exist
whether or not an escrow account is maintained. They arise from the security instrument you sign at closing and from the law of NY, and a failure to
meet them can result in a lien with priority over the mortgage, in an uninsured loss, or in charges assessed to your account. The notice is provided as of
November 14, 2024 for your reference. This document does not require a response from you unless it expressly states otherwise.

Article I. Property Taxes
General real estate taxes are assessed by the county or municipality in which the property lies and are billed on a cycle established by local law. Unpaid taxes
become a lien on the property that generally takes priority over the mortgage, and continued nonpayment can result in a tax sale of the property or of the tax
lien itself, in either case on a timetable set by statute rather than by the lender.

Where an escrow account is maintained, the servicer pays the general tax bill from escrow. You should nonetheless review each assessment notice and tax bill
you receive to confirm that the assessed value, the exemptions applied, and the parcel identification are correct. An error in any of those items affects the
amount escrowed and is corrected through the assessor, not through the servicer.

Article II. Exemptions and Appeals
Many jurisdictions offer exemptions that reduce the taxable value of an owner-occupied residence, and additional relief is frequently available to older
homeowners, to veterans, and to persons with disabilities. Exemptions are not automatic; they typically require an application within a filing window, and some
must be renewed. Filing promptly after closing avoids the loss of a year's benefit.

If you believe the assessed value of the property is excessive, most jurisdictions provide an appeal process with a defined deadline following the annual notice
of assessment. A successful appeal reduces the tax and, where an escrow account is maintained, reduces the escrow payment at the next analysis. Neither
the lender nor the servicer files exemption applications or appeals on your behalf.

Article III. Effect on Your Loan Documents
This document supplements the note, the security instrument, and the disclosures furnished to you in connection with loan number 1234567890. It does not
enlarge, reduce, or otherwise modify the amounts payable, the interest rate, the payment schedule, or any right or remedy established by those instruments,
and no statement here should be read as a representation that any particular term applies to your transaction.

Where this document summarizes a statute, a regulation, or a program requirement, the summary is provided for convenience. In the event of any difference
between the summary and the authority summarized, the statute, regulation, or program requirement controls, and no summary in this document limits any
right afforded to you by law.

Article IV. Required Hazard Insurance
The security instrument requires that the improvements be insured against loss by fire, hazards within the term "extended coverage," and other hazards for
which insurance is required, in the amounts and for the periods required, with a carrier acceptable to the lender. The policy must name the lender and its
successors and assigns as mortgagee so that notice of cancellation is received and the lender's interest is protected.

Coverage must be maintained continuously. A policy cancelled for nonpayment, not renewed at expiration, or reduced below the required amount leaves the
collateral unprotected and permits the servicer to place coverage at your expense after the notices described in the separate lender-placed insurance notice.
Confirm at each renewal that the mortgagee clause names the current servicer at the current address.

Article V. Language Access
This document is provided in English. If English is not your primary language, you may wish to have it reviewed with the assistance of a translator or an adviser
of your choosing before you rely upon it. Where we make a translated version of a document available, the translation is furnished as a courtesy; unless
applicable law provides otherwise, the English version governs the rights and obligations of the parties.

Free language assistance is available through the housing counseling organizations identified in the notice furnished to you concerning the availability of
counseling, many of which offer services in multiple languages. If you require assistance in communicating with us about loan number 1234567890, call (555)
555-0120 and identify the language you prefer so that we may make appropriate arrangements.

Article VI. Electronic Delivery of This Document
Where you have consented to receive records electronically, this document may be delivered to the electronic address on file or posted to a secure site with
notification to you, and such delivery satisfies any requirement that it be provided in writing. You may withdraw that consent at any time, and you may request a
paper copy of this or any other document delivered electronically, in each case in the manner described in the electronic records consent furnished to you.

If you are unable to access, view, or retain a document delivered electronically, notify us at (555) 555-0120 so that a paper copy may be sent to your address of
record. A request for a paper copy of a particular document is not, by itself, treated as a withdrawal of your consent to electronic delivery of other
communications.
