Article VII. Questions and Contact Information
General questions concerning loan number 1234567890 may be directed to ABC Mortgage Company by telephone at (555) 555-0120 during normal business
hours, or in writing at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY 12345. Please reference the loan number and the property address in every written communication so that
your correspondence is matched to the correct file without delay, and retain a copy of anything you send together with a note of the date it was sent.

Certain submissions must be sent to a specific designated address in order to receive the treatment that law prescribes, including a written notice of asserted
error, a request for information, and a request to exercise a privacy election. Where a designated address applies, it is identified on your periodic statement and
in the corresponding notice; using the general correspondence address for such a submission may result in a slower response.

Article VIII. Flood and Other Specialized Coverage
Where the property is located in a special flood hazard area, flood insurance is required by federal law for the term of the loan, in an amount at least equal to
the lesser of the outstanding principal balance, the insurable value of the improvements, or the maximum available under the National Flood Insurance
Program. The determination applicable to your property is disclosed to you separately.

Depending on the location and characteristics of the property, other coverage may be required or advisable, including windstorm or named-storm coverage in
coastal areas, earthquake coverage where the exposure warrants it, and a walls-in policy where a condominium or homeowners association maintains a
master policy. Review the association's coverage where applicable to confirm what it does and does not insure.

Article IX. Adequacy of Coverage
The dwelling limit should be sufficient to rebuild the structure at current construction costs, which may differ substantially from the purchase price or the
assessed value. Review the limit annually, and consider whether an extended or guaranteed replacement cost endorsement is appropriate. Review the
deductible as well, particularly any percentage deductible applicable to wind, hail, or named storms.

Consider also whether your personal property limits, loss-of-use coverage, and liability limits are adequate for your circumstances. Those coverages protect
you rather than the lender and are not addressed by the minimum requirements of the security instrument. An insurance professional can evaluate the
adequacy of coverage on 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345.

Article X. No Legal, Tax, or Financial Advice
This document is furnished for informational purposes and summarizes requirements, policies, or procedures in general terms. It does not constitute legal, tax,
accounting, insurance, or investment advice, and neither ABC Mortgage Company nor any of its employees or agents is acting as your adviser in any of those
capacities. Statements made here are necessarily general and may not address the particular facts of your situation.

You should consult your own attorney, tax adviser, insurance professional, or financial adviser regarding the application of the matters described here to your
circumstances, including the deductibility of interest and taxes, the adequacy of insurance coverage on the property, and the effect of the transaction on your
estate or financial planning. The cost of such advice is modest relative to the size of a residential mortgage obligation.

Article XI. Events Beyond Our Control
Neither party is liable for a failure or delay in performing an obligation under this document to the extent the failure or delay results from a cause beyond that
party's reasonable control, including an act of God, a natural disaster, a fire, an epidemic, an act of war or terrorism, a civil disturbance, a labor dispute, a
failure of telecommunications or utility service, or an action of a governmental authority.

This provision does not excuse the obligation to pay money when due, and it does not extend a deadline established by statute or regulation except to the
extent that authority itself provides relief. Where a widespread disruption affects a community, relief programs are frequently announced by regulators or by
loan program sponsors, and we administer any such program according to its terms.

Where an event of this character affects our ability to answer telephones, process mail, or deliver documents on the ordinary schedule, we will restore normal
service as promptly as practicable and will handle matters delayed by the disruption without penalty to you where the delay was not attributable to you.

Article XII. Handling of Loss Proceeds
Report a loss to your carrier promptly and notify the servicer, because the security instrument gives the lender an interest in insurance proceeds. Where a loss
is significant, proceeds are commonly issued jointly to you and to the servicer and are disbursed against the progress of repairs under a loss-draft process that
requires documentation such as the adjuster's report, contractor estimates, and inspections.

The purpose of that process is to ensure that proceeds are used to restore the collateral. It is administered under the terms of the security instrument and
applicable law. Contact the servicer as soon as a loss occurs so that the requirements are understood before repairs begin and so that disbursements are not
delayed by missing documentation.

Article XIII. Notifying the Servicer
Notify the servicer promptly of any change in insurance carrier, policy number, coverage amount, or agent; of any notice of cancellation or nonrenewal; of any
delinquent tax notice; and of any change in your mailing address. Notices sent to a stale address are still effective under the loan documents, so keeping the
address current is a practical protection.

Questions about the obligations described in this notice may be directed to ABC Mortgage Company at (555) 555-0120 or at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY
12345, referencing loan number 1234567890. This notice summarizes the security instrument and applicable law; where a difference exists, the security
instrument and the law control.

Article XIV. Delivery and Receipt of Communications
A communication we send to you is effective when mailed by first-class mail, postage prepaid, to the most recent address shown in our records, or, where you
have consented to electronic delivery, when transmitted to the electronic address on file or posted to the secure site with notification to you. Effectiveness does
not depend upon your having opened, retrieved, or read the communication, and a communication returned undeliverable remains effective as of the date it
was sent unless applicable law provides otherwise.

Where more than one person is obligated on loan number 1234567890, a communication delivered to any one of you is treated as delivered to all of you. A
communication you send to us is effective when actually received at the address designated for that category of communication; correspondence sent to a
payment remittance address or to an office not designated to receive it may be delayed and, for certain regulated submissions, may not start the response
period at all.

Article XV. If Taxes or Premiums Go Unpaid
Where an obligation on the property goes unpaid, the security instrument permits the lender to advance the funds necessary to protect its interest, including
paying delinquent taxes or purchasing insurance coverage, and to recover the advance from you together with interest at the rate provided in the loan
documents. An advance of that kind is added to the amount you owe.

An advance is a remedy of last resort rather than a service, and it is materially more expensive than paying the obligation yourself. Where an escrow account
exists, advances are rare because the servicer pays the escrowed items directly; where no escrow account exists, the responsibility to monitor and pay each
bill rests entirely with you.

Article XVI. Year-End Tax Information
Following each calendar year, the servicer furnishes a statement of the mortgage interest you paid, together with information about points and, where the
servicer disbursed them, real estate taxes paid from escrow. The statement is furnished by the deadline the Internal Revenue Service prescribes and is also
reported to that agency.

The deductibility of mortgage interest and property taxes depends on your individual circumstances and on limits established by tax law. The servicer reports
amounts; it does not advise on deductibility. Consult your own tax adviser regarding the treatment of the amounts shown on the statement for the property at
456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345.

Article XVII. Compliance With Applicable Law
This document and the transaction it concerns are subject to the federal statutes and regulations governing residential mortgage credit and to the law of the
State of NY. Where federal law preempts or supplements state law as to a particular matter, federal law controls as to that matter; where state law affords you a
greater protection that is not preempted, that protection applies.

If a change in law or regulation requires a provision of this document to be modified, the provision is deemed amended to the minimum extent necessary to
bring it into compliance, and the remainder continues in effect. No provision should be construed to require any act that applicable law prohibits, or to prohibit
any act that applicable law requires.

Article XVIII. If the Property Is Damaged
Report damage to your insurance carrier promptly, document the condition with photographs before repairs begin, and retain every estimate, invoice, and
receipt. Notify the servicer as well, because the security instrument gives the lender an interest in the proceeds and, for a significant loss, a loss-draft process
governs how funds are released.

Continue making your monthly payments while a claim is pending. A casualty does not suspend the obligation to pay, and the two matters are handled on
separate tracks; allowing the loan to fall behind while a claim is processed creates a second problem without resolving the first.

Qualified Written Request Procedures
IMPORTANT NOTICE — QUALIFIED WRITTEN REQUEST PROCEDURES
Loan #1234567890 · ABC Mortgage Company · 12/02/2024
Form No. MTG-5110 · Edition 1.0 · Issued 03/04/2024



This document does not require a response from you unless it expressly states otherwise. Federal servicing regulations give John Doe the right to
submit a written notice of asserted error and a written request for information concerning loan number 1234567890, and they require the servicer to
acknowledge and respond within defined periods. This document identifies the exclusive address for such submissions, describes what a qualifying
notice or request must contain, states the deadlines that apply, and explains the protections that attach while a submission is pending. These
procedures apply for the life of the loan secured by the property at 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345 and should be retained for future reference.

(a) Exclusive Address for Submissions
A notice of error or a request for information must be sent in writing to the address the servicer designates for that purpose. The designated address is stated
on your periodic statement, on the servicer's website, and in the notice of transfer of servicing where servicing changes. A submission sent to any other
address, including a payment remittance address, may not trigger the regulatory deadlines.

Written submissions concerning loan number 1234567890 should be directed to ABC Mortgage Company at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY 12345 unless a
different designated address has been provided to you in writing. Telephone conversations, while often the fastest way to resolve a routine question, do not
invoke the procedures described in this document, which apply only to written submissions.

(b) Authorization to Verify Information
You authorize ABC Mortgage Company, and any assignee or servicer of loan number 1234567890, to verify the information you have provided in connection
with the transaction, including by obtaining consumer reports, verifying employment and income, confirming deposit and asset balances with the institutions
holding them, obtaining tax return transcripts where you have executed the applicable authorization, and confirming the existence and terms of insurance
coverage on the property.

Verification may occur at any time during the origination of the credit and again before closing, and information obtained through verification is used in
evaluating the credit request and in servicing the account thereafter. Information collected in this manner is handled in accordance with the privacy notice
furnished to you and with applicable federal and NY law.

(c) What a Notice of Error Must Contain
A qualifying notice of error must state the name of the borrower, information that enables the servicer to identify the account, and the error asserted. It need not
be submitted on any particular form and need not use the words "notice of error," but it must describe the error with enough specificity that the servicer can
investigate the matter. A general expression of dissatisfaction is not a notice of error.

Covered errors include failing to accept a payment that conforms to the servicer's written requirements, failing to apply an accepted payment properly, failing to
credit a payment as of the date of receipt, failing to make a timely escrow disbursement, imposing a fee or charge without a reasonable basis, failing to provide
an accurate payoff balance, and any other error relating to the servicing of the loan.

(d) What a Request for Information Must Contain
A request for information must state the name of the borrower, information that enables the servicer to identify the account, and the information sought. A
request may seek documents such as a payment history, an escrow analysis, a copy of the note, or the identity of the owner or assignee of the loan. A request
seeking the identity of the owner or assignee is subject to a shorter response deadline than other requests.

A servicer is not required to respond to a request that is overbroad or unduly burdensome, to one that seeks confidential, proprietary, or privileged information,
to one that is irrelevant to the servicing of the loan, or to one that is duplicative of a request already answered. Where a response is declined on one of those
grounds, the servicer notifies you in writing and states the basis.

(e) Language Assistance
This document is provided in English. If English is not your primary language, you may wish to have it reviewed with the assistance of a translator or an adviser
of your choosing before you rely upon it. Where we make a translated version of a document available, the translation is furnished as a courtesy; unless
applicable law provides otherwise, the English version governs the rights and obligations of the parties.

Free language assistance is available through the housing counseling organizations identified in the notice furnished to you concerning the availability of
counseling, many of which offer services in multiple languages. If you require assistance in communicating with us about loan number 1234567890, call (555)
555-0120 and identify the language you prefer so that we may make appropriate arrangements.

(f) Questions and Contact Information
General questions concerning loan number 1234567890 may be directed to ABC Mortgage Company by telephone at (555) 555-0120 during normal business
hours, or in writing at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY 12345. Please reference the loan number and the property address in every written communication so that
your correspondence is matched to the correct file without delay, and retain a copy of anything you send together with a note of the date it was sent.

Certain submissions must be sent to a specific designated address in order to receive the treatment that law prescribes, including a written notice of asserted
error, a request for information, and a request to exercise a privacy election. Where a designated address applies, it is identified on your periodic statement and
in the corresponding notice; using the general correspondence address for such a submission may result in a slower response.

(g) Acknowledgment and Response Deadlines
The servicer must acknowledge receipt of a notice of error or a request for information in writing within five (5) business days, excluding legal public holidays,
Saturdays, and Sundays. For a notice of error, the substantive response is due within thirty (30) business days, subject to a fifteen-business-day extension in
most cases where the servicer notifies you of the extension and the reason for it.

Shorter deadlines apply to particular categories. An assertion that the servicer failed to provide an accurate payoff balance must be answered within seven (7)
business days, and a request for the identity of the owner or assignee of the loan must be answered within ten (10) business days. An asserted error
concerning a scheduled foreclosure sale must be answered before the sale or within the general period, whichever is earlier.

(h) Third-Party Service Providers
We engage third parties to perform functions in connection with the origination and servicing of residential mortgage loans, including document preparation,
data processing, payment processing, tax and flood determination services, insurance tracking, appraisal management, printing, and mailing. Those providers
receive only the information necessary to perform the service for which they are engaged.

Each provider is bound by contract to maintain the confidentiality and security of the information disclosed to it and to use that information only for the purposes
of the engagement. Engaging a service provider does not relieve us of responsibility for the performance of the function delegated, and inquiries concerning
any such function may be directed to us rather than to the provider.

(i) How the Servicer Responds
In responding to a notice of error, the servicer must either correct the error and notify you in writing of the correction, the effective date, and the contact
information for further assistance, or conduct a reasonable investigation and notify you in writing that no error occurred, stating the reasons and how you may
request the documents relied upon. Those documents are provided without charge upon request.

A response to a request for information provides the information sought and contact information for further assistance, or explains that the information is not
available, states why, and identifies the contact for follow-up. Responses are sent to the address of record unless you designate another address in your
submission.

(j) Protections While a Submission Is Pending
For sixty (60) days after receiving a notice of error concerning an asserted payment error, the servicer may not furnish adverse information to any consumer
reporting agency regarding the payment that is the subject of the notice. This protection applies to the specific payment disputed and does not suspend the
obligation to make other payments as they come due.

Submitting a notice of error or a request for information does not extend a payment due date, waive a late charge properly assessed, or suspend the accrual of
interest. It does obligate the servicer to investigate and respond, and it creates a documented record of the issue that is useful if the matter is later escalated to
a regulator.

(k) Telephone Communications and Call Monitoring
Telephone calls between you and ABC Mortgage Company may be monitored or recorded for quality assurance, training, and recordkeeping purposes, and
you consent to that monitoring and recording by continuing with a call after being advised of it. Recordings are retained in accordance with our records
schedule and are used only for the purposes described here and as applicable law otherwise permits or requires.

By providing a telephone number in connection with this transaction, you agree that we, our affiliates, our agents, and our service providers may contact you at
that number regarding the account, including by using an automatic dialing system or a prerecorded or artificial voice, and by text message, to the extent
permitted by applicable law. Message and data rates charged by your carrier may apply to any text message you receive.

You may withdraw consent to be contacted at a particular number, or ask that we use a different number or another method entirely, by notifying us at (555)
555-0120 or in writing at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY 12345. Withdrawing consent for automated calls does not prevent us from delivering the notices that
law requires, which may still be sent by mail or by another permitted method.

(l) Practical Guidance for Submissions
Submit a separate writing for each matter rather than combining several unrelated issues, state the loan number and property address at the top, describe the
facts in chronological order, identify the specific dates and amounts involved, and enclose copies of the supporting documents. Keep a copy of everything you
send, and send by a method that provides evidence of delivery.

Do not include a notice of error on or with a payment coupon or check, because payment processing is automated and a notice enclosed with a remittance
may not reach the correct department. Where the matter is urgent, a telephone call to (555) 555-0120 in addition to, rather than instead of, the written
submission is often helpful.

(m) Credit Reporting
We may furnish information about the status and payment history of loan number 1234567890 to one or more consumer reporting agencies, and we do so in
accordance with the accuracy and dispute-handling requirements that federal law imposes on furnishers. Information furnished ordinarily includes the account
type, the date opened, the balance, the scheduled payment, and the payment status as of the reporting date.

If you believe that information we have furnished about this account is inaccurate or incomplete, you may notify us in writing at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY
12345, describing the item and the reason you believe it to be incorrect and enclosing any supporting documentation. We will investigate, report the results to
you, and correct any inaccuracy with each agency to which the information was furnished.

You may also dispute the item directly with the consumer reporting agency, which must generally conduct its own reasonable reinvestigation. Disputing with us
and with the agency are independent routes and may be used together; neither route requires payment of any fee, and no service can lawfully remove
information that is accurate and current.

(n) Changes to Your Contact Information
Notify us promptly of any change in your mailing address, telephone number, or electronic address, and of any change in the name in which the account is
held. Until we have received notice of a change and have had a reasonable opportunity to act upon it, we are entitled to rely on the information most recently
reflected in our records, and a communication sent to that information remains effective.

Keeping your information current matters most at exactly the moments it is easiest to overlook: after a move, after a change in marital status, after a change in
electronic mail provider, and after the transfer of servicing. Several of the notices described in the documents furnished to you carry response deadlines, and a
notice that does not reach you still starts the period it establishes.

(o) Severability
If any provision of this document is held by a court or other tribunal of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, that holding shall not affect
any other provision, and the remainder shall continue in full force and effect as though the offending provision had never been included. The parties intend that
each provision be severable and that this document be given effect to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law.

Where a provision is unenforceable only because it exceeds a limit imposed by law, it shall be deemed reduced or reformed to the maximum extent the law
permits and enforced as so modified, so as to give effect to the original intent to the greatest degree possible. Nothing in this document waives or limits any
right afforded to you by a mandatory provision of federal law or of the law of NY.

(p) Documents Relied Upon
Where the servicer determines that no error occurred, the response identifies the reasons for that conclusion and states that you may request the documents
relied upon in reaching it. A request for those documents must be answered within fifteen (15) business days, and the documents are provided without charge.

Certain material is excluded from that obligation, including confidential, proprietary, or privileged information such as internal analyses and communications
with counsel. Where a document is withheld on that basis, the response identifies that documents were withheld and states the ground, so that the scope of
what was provided is clear.

(q) No Professional Advice Provided
This document is furnished for informational purposes and summarizes requirements, policies, or procedures in general terms. It does not constitute legal, tax,
accounting, insurance, or investment advice, and neither ABC Mortgage Company nor any of its employees or agents is acting as your adviser in any of those
capacities. Statements made here are necessarily general and may not address the particular facts of your situation.

You should consult your own attorney, tax adviser, insurance professional, or financial adviser regarding the application of the matters described here to your
circumstances, including the deductibility of interest and taxes, the adequacy of insurance coverage on the property, and the effect of the transaction on your
estate or financial planning. The cost of such advice is modest relative to the size of a residential mortgage obligation.

(r) Timing Around a Loan Transfer or Payoff
A servicer's obligation to respond ends with respect to a submission received more than one year after the loan was discharged or after servicing was
transferred, and a submission received during that period is answered by the servicer to whom it is properly directed. Address a submission to the party that
serviced the account during the period in question.

Where a submission concerns a payoff figure and the loan has since been paid, the seven-business-day deadline applicable to payoff assertions continues to
govern. Retain your payoff statement, the remittance confirmation, and the paid-in-full acknowledgment, since those three documents resolve nearly every
question that arises after a loan is satisfied.

Rate Lock Terms, Extensions, and Expiration
ABC MORTGAGE COMPANY — RATE LOCK TERMS, EXTENSIONS, AND EXPIRATION
Loan #1234567890 · ABC Mortgage Company · 11/20/2024
Form MTG-5384 · Rev. 3.6 · Effective 12/21/2023



This document describes the policy of ABC Mortgage Company concerning interest rate lock-in agreements for residential mortgage transactions,
including the application identified as loan number 1234567890 for the property at 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345. A rate lock is a commitment,
for a stated period and subject to stated conditions, to make credit available to John Doe at a specified interest rate and point combination. The specific
rate, points, lock period, and expiration date applicable to your transaction, if a lock has been established, appear on the separate rate lock confirmation
issued to you; this policy explains the rules that govern locks generally. This document supersedes any earlier version of the same document furnished
to you.

1.0 Floating Versus Locking
Until a lock is established, the rate applicable to your transaction floats, meaning that the rate available to you moves with the market and is not determined
until a lock is taken or, at the latest, until the point at which the loan documents are prepared. A floating rate exposes you to the possibility of both improvement
and deterioration in pricing before closing.

Locking fixes the rate and points for the lock period, transferring the risk of market movement during that period to the lender, which manages the exposure
through its own hedging arrangements. Neither choice is inherently better; the decision depends on your tolerance for uncertainty, the time remaining before
closing, and the state of the market when the decision is made.

2.0 Lock Periods and Expiration
Locks are offered for defined periods, commonly thirty, forty-five, or sixty days, and longer periods are available for certain programs at a price that reflects the
additional exposure. The lock expires at the close of business on the expiration date shown on the confirmation. A lock must be valid on the date the loan is
funded, not merely on the date the documents are signed.

Select a lock period that accommodates the realistic timeline of your transaction, including underwriting, appraisal, title work, and any condition likely to require
time to satisfy. A lock period that is too short frequently results in an extension fee that exceeds what the longer period would have cost at the outset.

3.0 How a Lock Is Taken
A lock is established only when we confirm it in writing. An oral discussion of available pricing, a rate quoted in a marketing communication, a rate shown on an
initial Loan Estimate issued before a lock, and a rate discussed in general conversation are not locks and create no commitment. If you have not received a
written lock confirmation identifying the rate, the points, the lock period, and the expiration date, your rate is floating.

Establishing a lock generally requires a complete application, a property address, and a loan program selection, because pricing depends on program,
occupancy, property type, loan amount, credit score, and loan-to-value ratio. A change in any of those characteristics after a lock is taken may require the lock
to be repriced under the terms described below.

4.0 Fraud Awareness and Reporting
Mortgage transactions attract fraud, most commonly in the form of messages that appear to come from a lender, a settlement agent, or a real estate
professional and that direct funds to an account controlled by a criminal. We do not transmit wiring instructions by electronic message, and we do not change
previously issued remittance instructions by electronic message. Verify any such instruction by telephone at a number you have independently confirmed
before transferring funds.

Report a suspicious communication concerning loan number 1234567890 to us at (555) 555-0120 promptly, and preserve the message rather than deleting it.
If funds have already been transmitted, contact your financial institution immediately and ask that a recall be initiated; the prospects of recovery diminish
sharply within hours, and prompt action is by far the most important factor.

5.0 Lock Extensions
Where the transaction cannot close before expiration, an extension may be available for a fee that depends on the length of the extension and the market at
the time it is requested. An extension request should be made before the lock expires; a request made after expiration is treated as a relock rather than an
extension and is priced accordingly.

An extension preserves the locked rate and points and changes only the expiration date. Fees for extension, where charged, are disclosed to you before the
extension is applied and appear on the revised disclosures issued for the transaction where required by the integrated disclosure rules.

6.0 Expiration and Relock
If a lock expires and the loan has not closed, pricing reverts to the market. A relock is generally offered at the worse of the original locked pricing and the
current market pricing, a convention that prevents a lock from operating as an option to be abandoned when the market improves. The terms of any relock are
confirmed to you in writing before they are applied.

Where expiration results from a delay attributable to us rather than to you or to a third party, the circumstances are reviewed and an accommodation may be
extended. Requests for such review should be directed to the office identified at the end of this policy and should describe the sequence of events giving rise to
the delay.




                                                              Retain this document with your loan file records.                                             Page 1 of 4
7.0 Requests for Copies of Documents
You may request a copy of any document relating to loan number 1234567890 that we hold, including the note, the security instrument, the closing disclosures,
a payment history, or an escrow analysis. Requests should be made in writing at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY 12345 or through the secure channel identified
on your statement, and should identify the documents sought and the period they cover.

Copies of recent documents are ordinarily provided without charge. A reasonable fee may be assessed, to the extent permitted by applicable law, for a request
requiring historical research, for the reproduction of a voluminous record, or for expedited delivery; any such fee is disclosed to you before it is incurred, and
you may withdraw or narrow the request instead.

Certain requests are governed by the servicing rules described in the notice concerning error resolution and information requests, which impose specific
acknowledgment and response deadlines when the request is sent to the designated address. Using that address for a documentary request is generally to
your advantage.

8.0 Revisions
We may revise this document from time to time to reflect changes in applicable law, in regulatory guidance, or in our own procedures. Where a revision
materially affects your rights or obligations, we will furnish a revised document or a notice describing the change in the manner and within the time that
applicable law requires, and the revision will apply prospectively from its stated effective date.

A revision does not alter the note, the security instrument, or the payment terms to which you agreed, none of which may be changed except as those
documents expressly permit or by a written modification executed by you and by an authorized officer. The version of this document currently in effect may be
requested at any time from ABC Mortgage Company at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY 12345.

9.0 Consent to Verify
You authorize ABC Mortgage Company, and any assignee or servicer of loan number 1234567890, to verify the information you have provided in connection
with the transaction, including by obtaining consumer reports, verifying employment and income, confirming deposit and asset balances with the institutions
holding them, obtaining tax return transcripts where you have executed the applicable authorization, and confirming the existence and terms of insurance
coverage on the property.

Verification may occur at any time during the origination of the credit and again before closing, and information obtained through verification is used in
evaluating the credit request and in servicing the account thereafter. Information collected in this manner is handled in accordance with the privacy notice
furnished to you and with applicable federal and NY law.

10.0 Float-Down Features
Certain programs offer a one-time float-down permitting a locked rate to be adjusted downward if the market improves by a stated margin before a defined
point in the transaction. Where a float-down is available, its cost, the improvement threshold that triggers it, the deadline for exercising it, and the number of
times it may be used are stated in the confirmation.

A float-down must be exercised affirmatively; it does not operate automatically when the market improves. If your confirmation does not identify a float-down
feature, none applies to your lock, and a later improvement in market pricing does not alter the locked terms.

11.0 Effect of a Transfer of Servicing
The servicing of loan number 1234567890 — the collection of payments, the administration of any escrow account, and the handling of your inquiries — may
be transferred to another company at any time. A transfer of servicing is not a sale of your obligation to a different borrower and does not change the interest
rate, the payment amount, the maturity date, or any other term of the note or the security instrument.

Where servicing transfers, you receive a notice from the transferor at least fifteen (15) days before the effective date and a notice from the transferee within
fifteen (15) days after it, unless the transfer occurs in circumstances for which the law permits a combined or later notice. The notices identify both companies,
the date payments should begin going to the new servicer, and the telephone numbers at which each may be reached.

For sixty (60) days after the effective date of a transfer, a payment received by the prior servicer on or before its due date may not be treated as late merely
because it was sent to the wrong company. Even so, redirect your payments promptly, and update any automatic payment arrangement you maintain through
your own financial institution, since that arrangement is under your control rather than ours.

12.0 Lock Terms and Your Disclosures
Taking a lock is a permitted event for issuing a revised Loan Estimate reflecting the locked rate and any point or credit associated with it. The revised estimate
must be delivered no later than three business days after the lock is established. Points, lender credits, and rate-dependent charges become subject to zero
tolerance once the rate is locked.

The interest rate shown on your final Closing Disclosure is the locked rate, and the charges shown reflect the locked pricing. If you observe a discrepancy
between your lock confirmation and your disclosures, raise it before closing so that it can be reconciled while a correction remains straightforward.

and no statement here should be read as a representation that any particular term applies to your transaction.

15.0 No Commitment to Lend
A rate lock is not a loan approval, a commitment to lend, or a waiver of any condition. Credit approval remains subject to underwriting, to satisfactory title and
valuation, to verification of the information you have provided, and to the requirements of the applicable program and investor. A lock preserves pricing; it does
not guarantee that the transaction will close.

This policy is provided as of November 14, 2024 and may be revised prospectively. Questions concerning a lock on loan number 1234567890, or requests for
an extension or relock, should be directed to ABC Mortgage Company at (555) 555-0120 or in writing at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY 12345. In the event of
any conflict, the written lock confirmation issued to you controls.

16.0 Points, Credits, and Pricing
A quoted rate is inseparable from the points or credits associated with it. Paying discount points buys a lower rate; accepting a higher rate produces a lender
credit that offsets closing costs. Neither is inherently better, and the right choice depends on how long you expect to hold the loan and on the funds available
for closing.

When comparing offers, compare the rate, the points, and the total of lender charges together, on the same day and for the same lock period, since pricing
moves during the day and a quote taken on Tuesday is not comparable to one taken on Thursday. Your Loan Estimate presents these elements in a
standardized format for exactly that purpose.

17.0 Credit Reporting
We may furnish information about the status and payment history of loan number 1234567890 to one or more consumer reporting agencies, and we do so in
accordance with the accuracy and dispute-handling requirements that federal law imposes on furnishers. Information furnished ordinarily includes the account
type, the date opened, the balance, the scheduled payment, and the payment status as of the reporting date.

If you believe that information we have furnished about this account is inaccurate or incomplete, you may notify us in writing at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY
12345, describing the item and the reason you believe it to be incorrect and enclosing any supporting documentation. We will investigate, report the results to
you, and correct any inaccuracy with each agency to which the information was furnished.

You may also dispute the item directly with the consumer reporting agency, which must generally conduct its own reasonable reinvestigation. Disputing with us
and with the agency are independent routes and may be used together; neither route requires payment of any fee, and no service can lawfully remove
information that is accurate and current.

18.0 Confirmation and Recordkeeping
The written lock confirmation states the borrower and property, the loan program and term, the locked rate, the points or credit, the lock period, and the
expiration date. Review it when it arrives and report any discrepancy immediately, while the market data supporting the intended terms are still current and the
correction is straightforward.

Retain the confirmation with your file for loan number 1234567890 and bring it to closing. Where a question arises at the closing table about the rate or the
pricing, the confirmation is the document that resolves it, and having it in hand converts a potential delay into a brief comparison.

19.0 Market Conditions
Mortgage pricing responds to conditions in the secondary market for mortgage-backed securities, which move continuously during trading hours and react to
economic data, monetary policy, and broader market conditions. Pricing may be republished more than once in a single day when the market moves sharply.

Neither ABC Mortgage Company nor any originator can predict the direction of that market, and no statement about future pricing should be understood as a
prediction or a commitment. The decision to lock or to float belongs to you, and it is properly made on the basis of your own tolerance for the risk of a change
rather than on a forecast.

This notice is furnished by ABC Mortgage Company to John Doe in connection with loan number 1234567890 and the application for credit to be

3. Delivery Deadlines
We will deliver a copy of each written valuation promptly upon completion, or no later than three (3) business days before consummation of the transaction,

completed valuation from the appraiser or valuation provider, not from the date the report is signed or reviewed internally.

You may waive the requirement that copies be delivered three business days before consummation, provided the waiver is given at least three business days

to deliver copies without charge. A waiver granted in connection with loan number 1234567890 applies only to the timing of delivery and never to your

valuation to the electronic address on file or post it to the secure document portal associated with your application and notify you that it is available. If you have
not consented to electronic delivery, we will mail copies by first-class mail, postage prepaid, to your address of record. Delivery is complete when the document
is mailed or transmitted, regardless of when it is opened or retrieved.

9. Appraiser Independence
Federal appraiser-independence requirements prohibit any person with an interest in a mortgage transaction from influencing or attempting to influence the
development, reporting, result, or review of a valuation through coercion, extortion, bribery, intimidation, compensation, or instruction. Neither ABC Mortgage
Company nor any of its loan production personnel may select, retain, or compensate an appraiser on the basis of a predetermined value conclusion, and

These requirements do not prohibit you or ABC Mortgage Company from asking an appraiser to consider additional property information, to provide further
detail or explanation of the basis for a value conclusion, or to correct errors of fact appearing in the report. Requests of that character are permissible and are
documented in the loan file. Any person who believes that appraiser independence has been compromised in connection with the valuation of 456 XYZ
Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345 may report the matter to us and to the appropriate state appraiser regulatory agency.

10. Reconsideration of Value
If you believe that an appraisal delivered to you contains a factual error, relies on comparable sales that are not reasonably comparable, or omits information
that materially affects the opinion of value, you may request a reconsideration of value. A request should identify the specific item believed to be inaccurate,
explain why it is inaccurate, and, where the request concerns comparable sales, identify alternative sales you believe are more appropriate, together with the
address, sale date, and sale price of each.

We will forward a properly supported request to the appraiser or valuation provider for review and will communicate the outcome to you in writing. A
reconsideration of value is a request for professional review, not a negotiation, and the appraiser retains sole responsibility for the final opinion of value.
Submitting a request does not by itself extend any deadline applicable to your transaction, and we encourage you to submit any request promptly after you
receive the report so that the review may be completed without delaying your closing.

11. Use and Limitations of the Report
An appraisal is an opinion of market value prepared for the use of ABC Mortgage Company in evaluating the adequacy of the property as collateral. It is not a
home inspection, a structural or mechanical evaluation, a survey, a code-compliance review, a pest or environmental assessment, or a warranty of any kind
concerning the condition of the property. The appraiser's inspection, where one is performed, is visual and limited in scope, and it does not extend to areas that
are inaccessible, concealed, or obstructed at the time of the visit.

You should not rely upon the appraisal as a substitute for an independent inspection of 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345 performed by a qualified
professional of your choosing. ABC Mortgage Company does not adopt or warrant the appraiser's conclusions for any purpose other than its own credit
evaluation, and delivery of a copy to you under this notice does not create any duty on our part with respect to the condition, habitability, or suitability of the
property.

A second appraisal may be required by the loan program, by an investor, or by our own quality-control procedures, and in defined circumstances it is required

We may also perform an internal review of a valuation, which may take the form of a desk review, a field review, or an automated quality check. A review is an
evaluation of the appraiser's work rather than an independent opinion of value, and it is not itself a written valuation requiring delivery unless it develops its own
value conclusion, in which case it is delivered to you like any other valuation.

16. Understanding the Report
An appraisal report identifies the subject property, describes its physical characteristics and condition, states the highest and best use, and analyzes recent
sales of comparable properties with adjustments for differences in location, size, condition, age, and amenities. The reconciliation section explains how the
appraiser weighed the indications of value produced by the approaches applied.

Pay particular attention to the description of the subject property, since a factual error there — an incorrect room count, square footage, lot size, or condition
rating — carries through the entire analysis. Errors of that kind are the most common and the most readily corrected, and identifying one promptly is the most
useful thing a borrower can do with a delivered report.

(k) Information for Former Customers

Escrow Account Terms and Annual Analysis Statement
ABC MORTGAGE COMPANY — ESCROW ACCOUNT TERMS AND ANNUAL ANALYSIS STATEMENT
Loan #1234567890 · ABC Mortgage Company · 11/23/2024
Doc. LN-6069 · Version 3.1 · Effective Date 06/19/2023



This document does not require a response from you unless it expressly states otherwise. This disclosure explains how an escrow account is
established, funded, analyzed, and adjusted in connection with loan number 1234567890 and the property located at 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY
12345. An escrow account is a fund held by the servicer from which property taxes, hazard insurance premiums, and similar recurring charges are paid
on your behalf as they come due. The estimates used to establish your account appear on the initial escrow account statement furnished separately;
this document describes the rules that govern the account for the life of the loan, including the cushion permitted by law, the annual analysis, and the
treatment of surpluses and shortages.

§ 1. Purpose of the Escrow Account
An escrow account allows the annual cost of property taxes and insurance to be collected in monthly installments together with your principal and interest
payment, rather than in large periodic sums. The servicer holds those funds and disburses them to the taxing authority and to the insurance carrier on or before
the date each obligation becomes due, provided the account contains sufficient funds and the servicer has received the bill or the information necessary to pay
it.

Maintaining an escrow account protects both you and the holder of the security instrument. Unpaid property taxes can become a lien with priority over the
mortgage, and a lapse in hazard coverage leaves the property unprotected against loss. Because those risks are shared, escrow is required for many loan
programs and is offered as an option on most others.

§ 2. Escrowed Items
The items escrowed for your account are listed on the initial escrow account statement and typically include general real estate taxes, special assessments
levied by a taxing district, hazard or homeowners insurance premiums, and, where applicable, flood insurance premiums and mortgage insurance premiums.
Items that vary by jurisdiction, such as ground rent or a municipal service charge, may also be escrowed where the loan program requires it.

Charges that are not escrowed remain your direct responsibility. These commonly include homeowners association dues, utility charges, supplemental or
omitted tax assessments issued outside the ordinary billing cycle, and any insurance coverage you elect beyond what the security instrument requires. A
charge is not escrowed merely because a bill for it is received by the servicer, and the servicer will forward or return items it does not administer.

§ 3. Initial Funding and the Cushion
At closing, an initial deposit is collected so that the account will hold enough to pay each escrowed item when it first comes due. Federal law permits the
servicer to maintain a cushion of no more than one-sixth of the estimated total annual disbursements, which is equivalent to approximately two monthly escrow
payments. Some loan programs and some state laws permit a smaller cushion, and where they do, the smaller figure controls.

The amount of the initial deposit depends on the month of closing relative to the tax and insurance due dates in NY, and it is calculated so that the projected
low point in the account balance over the coming twelve months equals the permitted cushion. The specific figures for this transaction appear on your Closing
Disclosure and initial escrow account statement and are not restated in this document.

§ 4. The Yearly Analysis
At least once each year the servicer conducts an escrow account analysis, comparing the payments actually made from the account with those that were
projected and estimating the disbursements expected during the coming computation year. The analysis produces a new monthly escrow payment and an
annual escrow account statement showing the account history, the projected activity, and the resulting change to your total monthly payment, if any.

The annual statement is furnished to you at least thirty (30) days before the new payment amount takes effect. Escrow payments change most often because a
taxing authority has revised the assessed value or the rate applicable to the property, or because the insurance carrier has adjusted the premium at renewal.
Those amounts are set by third parties, and the servicer neither controls them nor profits from an increase.

§ 5. Identity Verification Requirements
Federal law requires all financial institutions to obtain, verify, and record information identifying each person who opens an account, in order to help the
government fight the funding of terrorism and money-laundering activities. When you apply for credit, we ask for your name, address, date of birth, and other
information that allows us to identify you, and we may ask to see a driver's license or other identifying document.

The information collected for this purpose is used to verify identity and is retained in accordance with applicable law. It is not used as a factor in evaluating
creditworthiness, and requesting identifying documentation is a routine step applied to every applicant rather than an indication of any concern about a
particular transaction.

§ 6. Surpluses and Shortages
A surplus exists when the analysis shows that the account holds more than the target balance plus the permitted cushion. Where the account is current and the
surplus is fifty dollars or more, it is refunded to you within thirty (30) days of the analysis; a smaller surplus may be refunded or credited against future
payments. A shortage exists when the balance is below the target but the account is not overdrawn; you may pay a shortage in a lump sum or allow it to be
collected over the following twelve months.




                                                             Retain this document with your loan file records.                                          Page 1 of 3
A deficiency exists when the account balance is negative. Depending on the size of the deficiency and the status of the account, the servicer may require
repayment in a single sum or spread the amount over two to twelve months as permitted by law. In each case, the annual escrow account statement identifies
the condition of the account, states the amount involved, and explains the option being applied for loan number 1234567890.

§ 7. Definitions Used in This Document
Unless the context plainly requires otherwise, "you" and "your" refer to John Doe and to any other person obligated on loan number 1234567890; "we," "us,"
and "our" refer to ABC Mortgage Company and to any successor, assignee, or servicer that acquires the loan or the right to service it; and "the property" refers
to the real property located at 456 XYZ Avenue, XYZ City, NY 12345 that secures the loan. "Applicable law" means the federal statutes and regulations
governing residential mortgage credit together with the law of the State of NY, in each case as amended from time to time.

"Business day" carries the meaning given to it by the particular statute or regulation under which a right or deadline arises, and the count therefore differs
among the documents furnished to you; where a specific count matters, it is stated in the section that establishes the deadline. "Loan documents" means the
note, the security instrument, and every rider, addendum, disclosure, and agreement executed or delivered in connection with the credit transaction described
above.

§ 8. Fraud Awareness and Reporting
Mortgage transactions attract fraud, most commonly in the form of messages that appear to come from a lender, a settlement agent, or a real estate
professional and that direct funds to an account controlled by a criminal. We do not transmit wiring instructions by electronic message, and we do not change
previously issued remittance instructions by electronic message. Verify any such instruction by telephone at a number you have independently confirmed
before transferring funds.

Report a suspicious communication concerning loan number 1234567890 to us at (555) 555-0120 promptly, and preserve the message rather than deleting it.
If funds have already been transmitted, contact your financial institution immediately and ask that a recall be initiated; the prospects of recovery diminish
sharply within hours, and prompt action is by far the most important factor.

§ 9. Timely Disbursement Obligation
The servicer must make escrow disbursements on or before the deadline for payment, or, where a jurisdiction offers a discount for early payment, on or before
the discount date, provided the account contains sufficient funds and the servicer has received the bill or other necessary information. Where the account is
short, the servicer may advance funds to prevent a lapse or a delinquency and may then collect the advance in accordance with applicable law.

Records of every escrow receipt and disbursement are maintained for the life of the loan and are summarized on the annual statement. You may request an
account history at any time. If servicing is transferred, escrow funds transfer with the loan, and the transferee servicer assumes the obligation to make timely
disbursements without interruption.

§ 10. Discontinuing an Escrow Account
Where the loan program and the terms of the security instrument permit, you may request that the escrow account be discontinued after the loan has seasoned
and the account is current. Eligibility generally depends upon the loan-to-value ratio, the payment history, the absence of any prior escrow deficiency, and any
applicable investor requirement. A request should be made in writing and referenced to loan number 1234567890.

If an escrow account is closed, any remaining balance is refunded to you within the period required by law and you assume direct responsibility for paying
taxes and insurance premiums as they come due. Failure to pay those items thereafter permits the servicer to reestablish an escrow account, to advance funds
to protect its interest, and to place insurance on the property at your expense as described in the separate notice concerning lender-placed coverage.

§ 11. Events Beyond Our Control
Neither party is liable for a failure or delay in performing an obligation under this document to the extent the failure or delay results from a cause beyond that
party's reasonable control, including an act of God, a natural disaster, a fire, an epidemic, an act of war or terrorism, a civil disturbance, a labor dispute, a
failure of telecommunications or utility service, or an action of a governmental authority.

This provision does not excuse the obligation to pay money when due, and it does not extend a deadline established by statute or regulation except to the
extent that authority itself provides relief. Where a widespread disruption affects a community, relief programs are frequently announced by regulators or by
loan program sponsors, and we administer any such program according to its terms.

Where an event of this character affects our ability to answer telephones, process mail, or deliver documents on the ordinary schedule, we will restore normal
service as promptly as practicable and will handle matters delayed by the disruption without penalty to you where the delay was not attributable to you.

§ 12. Effect of a Transfer of Servicing
The servicing of loan number 1234567890 — the collection of payments, the administration of any escrow account, and the handling of your inquiries — may
be transferred to another company at any time. A transfer of servicing is not a sale of your obligation to a different borrower and does not change the interest
rate, the payment amount, the maturity date, or any other term of the note or the security instrument.

Where servicing transfers, you receive a notice from the transferor at least fifteen (15) days before the effective date and a notice from the transferee within
fifteen (15) days after it, unless the transfer occurs in circumstances for which the law permits a combined or later notice. The notices identify both companies,
the date payments should begin going to the new servicer, and the telephone numbers at which each may be reached.

For sixty (60) days after the effective date of a transfer, a payment received by the prior servicer on or before its due date may not be treated as late merely
because it was sent to the wrong company. Even so, redirect your payments promptly, and update any automatic payment arrangement you maintain through
your own financial institution, since that arrangement is under your control rather than ours.



                                                             Retain this document with your loan file records.                                           Page 2 of 3
§ 13. Initial and Annual Statements
The initial escrow account statement is provided at settlement or within forty-five (45) days after the account is established. It itemizes the estimated taxes,
insurance premiums, and other charges expected to be paid from the account during the first twelve months, the anticipated disbursement dates, and the
amount of the cushion.

Thereafter an annual escrow account statement is provided within thirty (30) days after the end of each computation year. It shows the actual activity of the
past year against the projections, the projected activity for the coming year, the new monthly payment, and the reason for any change. Compare each annual
statement to the prior one so that a change in taxes or premiums is understood when it occurs rather than later.

§ 14. Raising a Concern
If you are dissatisfied with any aspect of the handling of loan number 1234567890, we ask that you first raise the matter with us by telephone at (555)
555-0120 or in writing at 100 ABC Plaza, XYZ City, NY 12345, describing the issue, the dates and amounts involved, and the resolution you seek. Most
concerns are resolved fastest at that level, and a written summary from you is the most reliable way to ensure the matter is understood as you intend it.

You may also, at any time and without first contacting us, submit a complaint to the federal consumer complaint system, to the state regulator having
jurisdiction over the institution in NY, or to the federal banking agency that supervises us. Raising a concern with us does not waive, shorten, or otherwise limit
any right you have to pursue the matter with a regulator or through any other remedy available at law or in equity.

§ 15. Changes in Taxes and Premiums
Escrow payments change because the underlying obligations change. A reassessment of the property, the expiration of an exemption, the addition of a special
assessment district, or a change in the millage rate alters the tax bill, and a change in coverage, deductible, carrier, or the general insurance market alters the
premium. The servicer collects what those third parties charge.

Because the annual analysis both recovers a past shortage and adjusts the going-forward payment, an increase in taxes or premiums often produces a
payment increase larger than the increase in the underlying bill for the first year and a smaller increase thereafter. The annual statement separates those two
components so the arithmetic can be followed.

§ 16. Escrow at Payoff or Transfer
When the loan is paid in full, any balance remaining in escrow after the final disbursements is refunded to you within the period required by law, and thereafter
you pay taxes and insurance directly. Confirm with the taxing authority and the insurer that future bills are directed to you rather than to the former servicer,
since a bill sent to the wrong party is a common source of a missed payment after a payoff.

When servicing transfers, escrow funds transfer with the loan and the transferee servicer must honor the terms of the existing account, including any payment
arrangement for a shortage. The transferee conducts its own analysis in the ordinary course, and a change in the payment following a transfer reflects that
analysis rather than the transfer itself.
